#2199. Veteran with 522 EFL caps backs Lincoln City 23-year-old for ‘a big future’

Lincoln City have fared fairly well in their first 13 games of the 2026/27 Championship season, sitting in 16th with 15 points to their name. The Imps spent on new players like Mikkel Ladefoged and Andrei Coubis in the summer, but among those to impress on the step up from League One has been Deji Elerewe.

Now, the 23-year-old centre-back has received high praise from defensive partner and EFL veteran Sonny Bradley. Speaking to the club’s official media, he said: “I recognised it before the first couple of weeks that he came in the door. I could tell straight away in training that he was a big lad. He was aggressive, he was ready to get stuck in and everything that he was asked to do, he could do comfortably.

“I recognised pretty early that he’s got a big future in the game. He’s had a great start to the season, but it’s just the start. With the mentality that he’s got, I’m pretty sure he’ll want to take it into the rest of this year and certainly into the second half of the season.”

Having made 522 EFL appearances across all three leagues, Sonny Bradley knows what he’s talking about when it comes to impressive young prospects. Lincoln City’s stand-in skipper has played alongside and come up against plenty of top talents across his storied career, so his praise of Elerewe comes as a glowing review.

After starting out at Charlton Athletic, Elerewe made a name for himself at Bromley and earned his move to Sincil Bank in the winter. He started encouragingly, but has really stepped up in the Championship.

Elerewe has played all but six minutes of the Championship campaign so far, locking down a starting spot. He’s among the league’s top 13% of centre-backs for defensive contributions (113) and ranks highly for his interceptions (21 – top 7%), aerial duels won (40 – top 11%) and touches in the opposition box (30 – top 4%).

The Imps ace has the physical stature and power to hold his own against big strikers and he serves as an aerial asset in both boxes. At 23, he is of the age and profile to kick on further and challenge himself at a higher level in the years to come.

Elerewe’s progress at his young age means that excitement over his future is more than justified. He has the physical profile to be a success at all levels, so it will be a case of rounding out his game both defensively and in possession to push to new heights.

Lincoln City will have the firm belief that Elerewe can become a high value asset in the transfer market in the years to come. He has quickly grown into an influential player at Sincil Bank, and that will bring admiring glances from clubs higher up in the food chain.

For now though, Elerewe will be focused on the task at hand with the Imps, where he is under contract until 2029. Alongside his own personal development, the goal for this season is to stay in the Championship, and the London-born defender can have a key part to play in that.

#2198. Celtic handed fresh agony as star who got away rewrites Eredivisie record books

Sizzling Sondre Orjaester tore up the Eredivisie record books on Sunday and handed Celtic an unwanted reminder of the winger who slipped through their grasp.

The Norwegian wide man was the star of the show as FC Twente demolished Excelsior 9-0, chalking up an astonishing FIVE assists in the rout. The remarkable haul is the highest assist tally recorded by a player in a single Eredivisie match this century and underlines the stunning form that has made Orjaester one of the hottest properties in Dutch football.

It's another painful "what if?" moment for Celtic as the Premiership champions continue to search for answers in a difficult campaign.

The Parkhead club kept close tabs on the former Sarpsborg flyer and pushed to land him during the January 2025 transfer window. But despite significant interest, a deal could not be agreed and Orjaester remained in Norway before eventually making the move to Twente.

Read more: Miffed Martin O'Neill bites back in Celtic BBC interview exchange

Celtic instead turned to familiar ground, bringing Jota back to Glasgow in a £10 million deal. However, the Portuguese winger suffered a serious setback when he picked up a long-term injury against Dundee United in April 2025.

That left the Hoops back in the market for reinforcements and, by the close of the summer transfer window, Michel-Ange Balikwisha and Sebastien Tounekti had arrived in a double deal worth around £10m.

Orjaester, meanwhile, was flourishing in the Netherlands.

The 22-year-old previously opened up on why he decided against a switch to the Scottish champions, insisting the style of football on offer elsewhere was a better fit for his development.

Speaking to De Twaalfde Man, he said: "I don't think the type of football played there suits me best.

"The Eredivisie has proven to be a very good platform for young players like me, and there are a lot of technically skilled players there.

"I didn't have much time to think about whether I wanted to go to FC Twente.

"Of course, I knew they were narrowly eliminated in the Europa League last season against Bodø/Glimt. Everyone I spoke to about the club talked about the fans and how Twente played."

While Celtic continue to wrestle with their current issues, Orjaester is producing the sort of numbers that justify the hype which surrounded him. And after rewriting the Eredivisie record books with a five-assist masterclass, the Norwegian has shown exactly why so many believed he could have been a star in green and white.

#2197. Cardiff City’s injury struggles continue as Brian Barry-Murphy confirms new blow for attacker

Cardiff City face West Ham on Wednesday night, the league’s highest scorers. It marks another tough game in a challenging run of fixtures, and the Bluebirds will be without forward Isaak Davies after a new injury blow.

Brian Barry-Murphy confirmed to BBC Sport Wales that Davies will face four weeks on the sidelines with a hamstring issue. Unfortunately for the City boss, the Welsh attacker is not the only concern, with Perry Ng and Alex Robertson in need of assessment while Dylan Lawlor, Calum Chambers, and Callum Robinson have been out too.

Robinson has been omitted from the last three matchday squads, but the decision has not been expanded on since Barry-Murphy first said ‘certain standards’ had not been met.

Aside from a loan spell in Belgium, Isaak Davies has always played for Cardiff City. He joined the club when he was seven, making his professional debut against Middlesbrough in October 2021 and scoring his first goal against Preston North End in January 2022.

Fans have a natural affection for the player because of his affiliation with the club. However, he has struggled to make a mark on the first team for the most part, and that has continued this term.

Davies has only played 74 minutes of Championship football so far this season, and he is yet to score. His highest goalscoring season for the Bluebirds is six goals, compared to 12 scored in a productive loan spell with KV Kortrijk.

He’s had injury absences to deal with too, impacting his bid to find consistency. It will be hoped this latest blow does not result in an extended spell on the sidelines with four weeks the initial timescale.

Although the news about Davies is a blow, defensive injuries are more of a concern at Cardiff City currently. The Bluebirds will operate with Yousef Salech up front and have the option of Jack Moylan should he be required.

However, defensively, they are without Lawlor, Chambers and Bielik, amongst others. It meant Barry-Murphy had to utilise Joel Colwill and Ollie Tanner as emergency full-backs at the end of the 3-0 defeat to Wolves.

Despite their defensive injuries, City haven’t done too badly at the back in terms of their performances. They have conceded 20 goals, less than nine other teams in the division.

The Bluebirds will be looking to take advantage of their upcoming fixtures, with games against the likes of Norwich City and Preston North End on the horizon. They will be hoping their injury problems ease as soon as possible to give themselves the best possible chance of taking the points in those matches.

#2196. Liverpool boss in astonishing admission - I will urge my players to dive

Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola says he will urge his players to dive in future after Alexander Isak was refused a penalty in Sunday’s 1-0 loss to Arsenal.

The Liverpool striker’s shirt was pulled by Jurrien Timber as he leapt to reach a cross into the box during the first half of the Premier League encounter at Anfield.

Isak did not go to ground and referee Andy Madley gave nothing. VAR Stuart Attwell also saw no reason to overturn the decision.

Asked if players should go down, Iraola said: “It’s a shame you ask me this question, but honestly, yes, we have to tell them, go down, because they’re not going to call it otherwise.

Read more: ‘Emotional’ Marink Reedijk enjoys post-match scenes as Hibernian book final spot

“And then referees complain why they go down. Because if you don’t go down, you don’t call it. Then it’s like, no, you are all the time going down.

“But I think Alex is honest. He tries to go for the ball, everyone can see live straight away there is a clear, clear pull.”

He added in a BBC interview: “The answer is you have to dive. If you don’t dive they are not going to call it.”

The incident occurred soon after Arsenal had taken the lead in the 16th minute as Kai Havertz benefited from an Alisson Becker error.

Liverpool went on to dominate for large spells but could not break Arsenal’s resilience.

Florian Wirtz did hit the bar from a free-kick and Cody Gakpo also had a penalty appeal turned down after a tussle with Christos Tzolis but Iraola was less concerned about that decision.

He said: “The Gakpo one, I think it’s a sustained holding but I understand their argument and I think they are right that they say the ball was too long and Cody wouldn’t have arrived to the ball.

“I think we have to blame the start of the game. Until we conceded the goal, (we were not) at the level of the rest of the game. But from 1-0, I loved the reaction of the team.”

Arsenal’s victory was their first at Anfield in the league for 14 years and took them to the top of the table.

Manager Mikel Arteta said the champions were motivated by a desire to bounce back from their shock Carabao Cup loss to League Two Fleetwood in midweek.

Arteta said: “It has been such a long time without having this winning feeling here.

“We are extremely proud of the team and the players and what everyone has done, especially in the conditions in which we arrived to this game – the defeat against Fleetwood looks the end of the world, but then you have to pick yourself up.

“How the hell can you go out of the cup when you shoot 27 times and have the chances we had against a team who had one shot on target? Then you look so silly but I had the feeling now was the moment.”

#2195. Under-fire figure eyed Leicester City boss Russell Martin for top Premier League job in 2024

Leicester City hired Russell Martin in the summer, bringing him in to lead their rebuild after relegation from the Championship. The LCFC boss has faced criticism for inconsistent performances and a frustrating style of play, but it wasn’t long ago that he was held in very high regard.

Martin’s work at MK Dons, Swansea City and in winning promotion to the Premier League with Southampton saw him build a strong reputation in the game. So much so, Manchester United sporting director Jason Wilcox – who worked with Martin at St. Mary’s – put him forward as a candidate to monitor when the Red Devils were considering their Erik ten Hag replacements in 2024.

Wilcox viewed Martin as someone to monitor and consider for the role in the future, rather than as an immediate option. This was shortly before the 2024 FA Cup final in May, so around the same time as the Championship play-off final, which the Saints won.

Wilcox moved from Manchester City to Southampton in 2023, stepping into a director of football role for the first time. He would hire Martin from Swansea City shortly after, and the two found success together.

With Martin as manager and Wilcox as a director, the Saints would win immediate promotion back to the Premier League. It saw the stocks of both surge, but the boss stayed put while Wilcox was tempted away to become technical director in a new-look Manchester United hierarchy, before seeing his title switched to director of football.

Neither have found the same fortunes since though. Martin was eventually sacked by Southampton as they sat bottom of the Premier League table, and a dismal 17-game spell at Rangers led to his next managerial opportunity coming in League One with Leicester City.

Wilcox meanwhile remains at Manchester United, but he has been under-fire for shortcomings in recruitment. Many supporters pin their continued struggles on him, and he was in the line of fire when defender Lisandro Martinez called out the club hierarchy too.

Managerial stock comes and goes, and few have experienced the highs and lows quite like Martin. His work in rebuilding Southampton and getting them promoted earned rave reviews, and rightly so.

However, he stuck by his playing principles on the step up to the Premier League, and it backfired badly. Some would argue he has never really recovered from that, with criticisms over his playing style following him to Rangers and Leicester City, and his willingness to speak up and stick to his guns while speaking to the press brings ridicule.

Despite this, he is still a young manager at only 40, and his CV shows how he can rebuild struggling clubs and build a philosophy for fans, players and staff alike to buy into.

Martin is trying to replicate his past success at Leicester City. He faces an uphill battle to do so, but that will not deter him as both he and LCFC fight to return to their previous heights.

#2194. West Ham backed to seal ‘dream’ appointment of man Sir Alex called ‘incredible’

This article is part of Football League World's 'Terrace Talk' series, which provides personal opinions from our FLW Fan Pundits regarding the latest breaking news, teams, players, managers, potential signings and more…

Pressure is mounting on Nuno Espírito Santo after back-to-back home defeats in the Championship.

The Hammers were beaten comprehensively by fellow promotion candidates West Brom last weekend, with fierce criticism directed at the West Ham boss for their struggles.

Despite being backed to win the division convincingly and return to the Premier League at the first time of asking, the East London outfit have struggled to assert their dominance, with consecutive losses in front of their own supporters leaving the club languishing in eighth – a position nowhere near acceptable for the level of quality their squad possesses.

And it’s raising big questions about whether a change in the dugout is needed, with such slowness out of the traps contributing to their demise.

One of those candidates who could be in a strong position to replace Nuno is Kieran McKenna, who departed Ipswich Town at the end of last season to take a break from management.

But a few months on after guiding the Tractor Boys back to the Premier League, he may be interested in the challenge of managing such a big club like the Hammers, so it’s a deal that could be very much on the cards.

So with this in mind, FLW’s West Ham fan pundit has commented on the recent speculation surrounding McKenna and whether he would welcome the 40-year-old to the London Stadium.

It’s safe to say that Nuno’s position at West Ham is becoming increasingly bleaker, with the Hammers reportedly considering a change in the dugout following an unexpectedly poor start on their Championship return.

Successive defeats at home to Southampton and West Brom has left many connected with West Ham fearing that Nuno isn’t the man to lead the club back to the promised land of the Premier League and that a change is needed in order for the club to get back competing towards the automatic promotion places.

And according to journalist Alan Nixon, West Ham have drawn up a three-man managerial shortlist of candidates should they decide to part ways.

It is believed that the shortlist consists of Kieran McKenna, Rob Edwards and Scott Parker, who are all out of work and possess previous experience of getting clubs promoted from the Championship to the Premier League.

So with this development, FLW’s West Ham fan pundit has reacted to McKenna being linked with a move to the club.

Speaking to Football League World, West Ham fan pundit Ryan Horn has urged the Hammers to appoint Kieran McKenna to replace Nuno, insisting he would be the ‘perfect fit’ for the club to move towards a more front-footed and modern style of play.

When asked whether he would like to see Kieran McKenna become the new West Ham boss, Ryan told FLW: “100%. I think Kieran McKenna should be who we go for.

“I know he’s taken some time out for personal reasons, I believe, and I know he’s studying some stuff with UEFA to up his game, but I think what he brings is something that the older style managers like Nuno, (Sean) Dyche, maybe (David) Moyes just don’t have in their locker, that modern-day footballing approach.

Five players, five careers. Name them from the clubs they played for.

Each day there are five current or former EFL players to identify. For each one you’ll see their senior clubs in the order they played for them. Loan spells are left out.

You get four guesses per player. Every wrong guess unlocks a clue: first their position, then their nationality, then their initials.

Get it first time for 4 points, then 3, 2 and 1. The best possible score is 20. A new set of players arrives at midnight.

“The game has changed so much in the last decade, and we want to move from the old-style approach that West Ham have been on. We’ve been so sideways stepping, sometimes even backwards, when it comes to managerial choices.

“We should have gone for someone like McKenna after Moyes, not sidestepped backwards in a way to Lopetegui, but now, with Nils Koppen, Mark Noble and the changes around the board that are still coming into play, I think this is a great time to bring in someone, back them and build a team for them because they have done it with less of a budget, less pressure in a way, other than by pressure from their own fans.

“Ipswich fans loved McKenna, he did such a great job there, and I think he’d be the perfect fit for us. I think he’s one of those managers that can come in and have that Arteta effect at Arsenal, so yeah, I think McKenna replacing Nuno, that would be my dream, that’s the best outcome.

“Nuno needs to go either way, but we need to not make sidestep approaches like we’ve done in the past and McKenna is forward-thinking, has a modern-day footballing approach, and we haven’t had that at West Ham at all.”

Named an ‘incredible young talent’ by Sir Alex Ferguson during his early coaching days at Manchester United, Kieran McKenna has certainly lived up to all the hype and expectation, doing a fantastic job at Ipswich Town by leading them from League One all the way into the Premier League, as well as driving them back to the big time for a second time last season.

Not to mention McKenna achieved these incredible feats with Ipswich on a limited budget too, so working with much better players at the London Stadium and having the cash to bolster the squad in January are added bonuses that could see the Northern Irishman work wonders, should he be given the role.

West Ham fans, would you like to see Kieran McKenna replace Nuno at the London Stadium? Has his work at Ipswich Town convinced you enough that he can get the Hammers back into the Premier League? Comment below!

After some time away from management, McKenna may well be keen on getting his teeth stuck into another Championship project at the London Stadium, with West Ham always an appealing club given their size at this level.

McKenna’s modern style of play and way of working could be exactly what is needed to turn the West Ham ship around following an extended period of malaise under Nuno, with the rot clearly setting in and the Portuguese boss set for the exit door if these performances and results carry on for much longer.

If West Ham want to avoid seeing their promotion hopes go up in smoke, they must act quickly with McKenna still available, with the 40-year-old having every chance of delivering success to this football club given his previous exploits in Suffolk.

#2193. West Ham should appoint London-born boss if Nuno Santo is sacked

Nuno Espirito Santo's future at West Ham United is in serious doubt following consecutive home defeats to Southampton and West Bromwich Albion, and if he is fired there's one candidate who stands out from the rest.

The mood of the West Ham United faithful was very audible indeed at the end of their team's 3-1 home defeat to West Bromwich Albion on Saturday afternoon.

Boos echoed around an already half-empty London Stadium upon the final whistle at the end of a second home defeat in eight days, which dropped the Irons down to eighth place in the Championship table, leaving them four points from the division's automatic promotion places.

This result piled even greater pressure on the West Ham head coach Nuno Espirito Santo. Given that Santo was unable to keep the club in the Premier League at the end of the 2025-26 season, there had been some surprise that he remained in his position over the summer, but amid reports of a crisis meeting at which his future is to be discussed, talk is already turning to who might replace him and set their season back on track.

And while there will be suggestions for a replacement from all over Europe and possibly beyond, London-born Scott Parker, who played for West Ham and has already proven himself more than once in the Championship, stands out from the other potential candidates for the position.

When Nuno Espirito Santo was hired as the head coach at West Ham United on the 27th September 2025, the task ahead for him was clear. West Ham had just sacked Graham Potter and had lost four of their first five games of the season, a run which left them 19th in the Premier League. Santo's job was to keep the club in the Premier League.

But Santo did not keep West Ham in the Premier League. Results did pick up in the new year, and they went on a run which saw them lose just three times in 13 games between the middle of January and the end of April. But just when they needed that little nudge to get over the line, their form fell away again.

Three successive defeats to Brentford, Arsenal and Newcastle left them needing a win from their final home match of the season against Leeds United while hoping that Spurs lost at home to Everton. On this occasion, the West Ham players did rise to the occasion, winning 3-0, but a 1-0 win for Spurs against Everton rendered these efforts irrelevant. After 14 consecutive years of Premier League football, West Ham would be returning to the Championship.

Santo wasn't sacked and replaced over the summer, and some West Ham supporters might have questioned the wisdom of that non-decision when his team picked up just two points from their first three games, including a 2-1 home defeat to Charlton Athletic, but form did pick up, and by the time of their 6-0 win against Wrexham on the 11th September, they were top of the table.

But since then, they've only won two out of six, and two consecutive home defeats in eight days have turned the pressure back up under the embattled head coach. With the defeat to West Bromwich Albion coming on top of a 3-2 home loss to Southampton a week earlier, conceding six goals over two consecutive home matches is not something that West Ham fans would have been expecting to see this season. Coming on top of the relegation at the end of last season, the calls for Santo's departure have become impossible to ignore.

A slow start to West Ham's return to the Championship has turned the heat up under Nuno Espirito Santo, and Parker could be waiting in the wings.

As a big club in reduced circumstances, West Ham United require careful handling this season, but ahead of anything else they need a quick return to the Premier League. And this is where Scott Parker comes in. Parker was born in London and started his career with Charlton Athletic, but he also spent four years at West Ham from 2007 to 2011, scoring twelve goals and registering ten assists in 141 appearances for the club before signing for Tottenham Hotspur for £6 million.

Parker, then, has West Ham credentials, but he also has something else in his locker which should be of interest to the club's directors. Since entering the managerial game in 2019 with Fulham he has developed something of a reputation as a Championship specialist. Three times over the last seven years he's finished his season by leading a club into the Premier League, and that is the precise skill set that the club need at the moment.

​​​​​​In 2021, he returned Fulham to the Premier League through the play-offs, after they beat Brentford 2-1 in the Wembley final. Two years later at Bournemouth, he returned the Cherries to the top-flight as runners-up behind his former club, who'd been relegated back at the first attempt. And in 2025 he took Burnley back into the Premier League as runners-up behind Leeds United on goal difference, despite having run up 100 points with a team who conceded just 16 goals in 46 Championship games.

Three levels, ten questions each. Score at least 7 out of 10 to reach the next level. The first question is loading.

The issue with Parker has always been what happens once his teams get back to the Premier League. He was sacked by the end of the following season at all three of the clubs that he took up, and there's been little indication that his Championship credentials can be expanded to the peculiarities of the Premier League.

But Parker ticks a lot of boxes. For one thing, since he hasn't been in work since leaving Burnley shortly before the end of last season, he's available, meaning that hiring him would less expensive than having to pay compensation to another club. He's also a former West Ham player who knows the club.

And for the time being, the only thing that really matters in the first place is getting back into the top-flight. When West Ham were relegated last time, they did bounce back immediately, though it took the play-offs to get them there. Premier League parachute payments don't last forever, and every year that they don't get back up will be costing the club serious money.

London-born and with a history both with West Ham and of getting teams out of the Championship in an upward direction, Scott Parker could be an ideal solution for the club, should they decide that Nuno Espirito Santo has used up all of his chances at The London Stadium.

#2192. Newcastle kit fiasco sums up haphazard pre-season

Newcastle’s pre-season friendly against Bayer Leverkusen at St James’ Park took a bizarre turn when a kit clash prompted the hosts to change shirts midway through the first half.

The German team’s white away kit with blue trim proved hard to distinguish from Newcastle’s home strip, which has a white back and blue stripes across the shoulders.

During the first-half hydration break, Newcastle decided to change into their lilac third kit, which improved the viewing experience for fans who took to social media to question the original choice of kits.

Newcastle would go on to lose the game 2-1 in new manager Matthias Jaissle’s first game at St James’, a result which followed a 3-1 reverse against Everton on Wednesday evening.

Leverkusen, the 2023-24 Bundesliga champions now managed by Spaniard Carles Martínez Novell, scored after just 44 seconds through a powerful Ibrahim Maza strike.

Jaissle’s team found their feet as the first 45 minutes progressed, with Yoane Wissa their biggest attacking threat. The striker endured a difficult first season at the club, but his performances at the World Cup with DR Congo appear to have restored confidence.

Newcastle were level just before half-time, when Malick Thiaw rose highest to plant home a back-post header from a corner. Former Brentford goalkeeper Mark Flekken appealed in vain for a foul, but there was no infringement.

After changing all 10 outfield players at half-time against Everton, Jaissle was more circumspect with second-half substitutes; Rory Finneran for Lewis Miley was the only change before the 80th minute.

Newcastle faded though, and the game was won by Victor Boniface scoring just a few minutes after coming on as a substitute. The Nigeria striker wrong-footed Sean Steur with an impudent piece of skill before rolling the ball into the bottom corner.

The North-East club are coming to terms with the departures of Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali and Bruno Guimarães this summer, as well as manager Eddie Howe. They have one more pre-season friendly to play, against Strasbourg on Sunday, before they begin their Premier League campaign at home to Liverpool.

Newcastle United (4-2-3-1) Hornicek; M Miley (Pivas 81), Thiaw, Botman, Hall; Steur, L Miley (Finneran h-t); Elanga, Woltemade (Neave 86), Barnes; Wissa. Subs Charlton, Harris (g), Sanusi, Johnson.

Bayer Leverkusen (4-2-3-1) Flekken; Vazquez (Tape h-t), Bade, Tapsoba, Gutierrez (Belocian 70); Garcia, Fernandez (Terrier 70); Maza (Boniface 80), Tillman (Doganay 70), Moreira (Tella 80); Kofane (Schick h-t). Subs Hofmann, Arthur, Oermann, Poku, Blaswich (g), Alfa-Ruprecht, Hawighorst, Lomb (g).

Referee Michael Oliver (Durham). Attendance 39,059

A second pre-season defeat in a week for Newcastle. Just like against Everton, they faded in the second 45 minutes but Jaissle decided to leave some tired legs out there for fitness purposes. The performances of Barnes and Wissa were promising, but Newcaslte are giving up chances.

Newcastle had a free-kick with the last kick of the game, but Harvey Barnes loops the delivery straight into Flekken’s gloves.

Schik with a chance to wrap up the victory, but Hornicek saves before Thiaw clears to deny Terrier a tap in on the rebounds.

There will be just three minutes of added time to play.

Elanga fouled near the touchline, but time is running out. The free-kick won by Neave came to nothing.

Chance for Barnes! Good combination play involving Elanga and Wissa down the right, and the ball flashed across the six-yard box. Barnes almost steered it in, but did not make firm enough contact.

Newcastle attacking with more urgency since conceding, but there are moans and groans in the ground at a misplaced Elanga pass. Sean Neave has just replaced Woltemade, and the 19-year-old wins a free-kick in a crossing position with his first action of the game.

The striker has only been on the pitch a few minutes, but Boniface has restored Leverkusen’s lead. Lovely chop inside the box, which sent Steur for a hot dog, before passing the ball into the far corner. No celebration of note from a player who could be on the move this summer.

Newcastle making just their second change of the game: Pivas replaces Mason Miley at right-back.

Leverkusen have made two more changes: Moreira and Maza off, Tella and Boniface on.

The corner is straight down the throat of Flekken, and that prompsts some groans from the home fans.

Newcastle having to defend deep for long periods, but Elanga did well to win a free-kick with little support. Moreira dragged the winger down. Then Wissa’s cross is turned behind for a corner.

Woltemade’s control lets him down as he tries to bring the ball down on halfway. The game is being played at a snail’s pace at the moment, but Leverkusen are dominating the ball.

Play has now resumed. Garcia does well to defend after Lewis Hall won the ball back in a dangerous position.

Time for another hydration break and Leverkusen are making three more substitutions. We await further changes from Jaissle. Should the game finish level, there will be a penalty shoot-out to decide the winner of the Visit Malta Cup.

Rather like the mid-week friendly against Everton, Newcastle have faded after half-time. Struggling to get into the game in any meaningful way. Slick football from Leverkusen but Fernandez fails to bring the ball under his spell in the box when there was time and space to shoot.

Leverkusen just inches away from regaining the lead. It was an incisive run off the left from Afonso Moreira, who tried to place the ball into the far corner but his attempt rolled just wide of the post.

Good defensive header by Lewis Hall before Wissa wins a foul on halfway. Newcastle feeding off scraps at the moment. Elanga goes too early and is flagged offside.

Bayer Leverkusen have had the better of it in this half, but some of the shooting has been wayward. This time is it Schik’s turn to slash a shot over the bar. Fouls committed by Finneran and Botman.

Newcastle with a three-on-three on the break after Wissa does well to win the ball back on halfway, but Woltemade was too slow to get his shot away at the end of the move. More good play from Wissa.

Half a chance for Fernandez to shoot from the edge of the D, but he was leaning back and ballooned the shot miles over the bar.

Finneran, the youngster in Newcastle’s midfield, is caught on the ball but then does well to recover it. I reckon there will be a raft of changes on the hour mark.

Corner for Leverkusen after Moreira gets forward and attacks Mason Miley. The German side have additional aerial threat with Schik on the pitch. Woltemade does well to head clear.

Bayer Leverkuen kick off in the second half.

Jaissle made 10 against Everton, so wants his starters to build minutes today. Rory Finneran is coming on for Newcastle, an 18-year-old academy player. He replaces Lewis Miley in midfield. Czech striker Patrik Schik is on for Bayer Leverkusen.

The scoreline is a fair reflection of an even first half, with Wissa Newcastle’s best player. The story though, is that kit clash that prompted Newcastle to change into their lilac third kit halfway through the half.

Just the two minutes of stoppage time to play.

Newcastle equalise from a set-piece. Flekken is claiming a foul, but it is a legitimate goal. The goalkeeper was nowhere to be seen on a corner that looped all the way to be back post, and he seemed to lose his bearings allowing Thiaw to find the far corner.

Newcastle have a corner after another move in which Wissa was lively. His performances have been a ray of light in pre-season, he really struggled in his first season at the club.

Lewis Hall takes the free-kick, but he scoops it well over the bar. Elanga delivers a low cross from the right, but Garcia is well positioned to clear.

Newcastle enjoying a lot more possession now, but you cannot say they look like equalising.

That was better though, more zip in the attack with Elanga laying the ball off for Wissa and Fernandez is booked from dragging the Newcastle forward to the ground. Free-kick in a shooting position.

Good play from Lewis Hall, skipping beyond two challenges to escape from a tight spot but then his crossfield pass is intercepted. Moreira passes the ball straight out of play for a Newcastle goal kick, when there was a chance for Leverkusen to punish the hosts on the break.

Elanga tries to take on Gutierrez but his low cross is too close to Flekken. Gutierrez then buys a foul when under pressure from Lewis Miley. Game has become quite bitty following those stoppages. Maza then chops down Harvery Barnes.

The game is back under way. Changing kits has improved things visually but it is still not ideal. You wonder how on earth two clubs of this stature failed to liaise on this before the game.

Bayer Leverkusen are still on top, but play has been stopped for a hydration break. Some boos from the stands, it is not an especially hot day.

On the subject of the kit clash, Newcastle are now changing into their lilac away kit. Shades of Manchester United at the Dell all those years ago.

A short stoppage in play after Tapsoba receives a knock in the small of the back from Newcastle’s goalkeeper Hornicek. Both managers get their players over for a tactical conflab.

Leverkusen look very accomplished in possession, they are moving the ball well through the lines. Kofane was a big threat when they played Arsenal in last season’s Champions League and they are looking to find him with crosses. Mason Miley defends well at right-back, but at the expense of a corner.

Flekken called into action again, Newcastle starting to warm to their task. It was direct play from first Elanga and then Barnes, but his cross deflects towards the goalkeeper and he parries away. Then Barnes is fouled, and Newcastle have a free-kick in a crossing position near the left corner of the penalty area. Poor delivery from Barnes, Flekken claims.

Newcastle fans sing “walking in a Keegan wonderland” in unison. Bade is then penalised for catching Woltemade late as they contested an aerial challenge.

Newcastle’s best moment so far: Wissa peels off the shoulder of Bade and tested Flekken with a volley from a tight angle. The goalkeeper saved and Leverkusen scramble clear, but it was good movement from the Newcastle striker.

Leverkusen continue to make the running, enjoying more possession and most of it is coming inside Newcastle’s half. Goalkeeper Flekken takes a beat inside his own six-yard box, and his pass out is almost cut out by Woltemade.

Newcastle’s players are wearing black armbands in memory of Kevin Keegan.

There is a slightly awkward clash of kits on display: both shirts feature a lot of white, and the blue trim around the shoulders of Newcastle’s home kit is quite similar to Leverkusen’s away strip.

Kofane, who impressed up front last season in Germany, throws himself at a cross.

Fans were barely settled in their seats when Maza’s vicious left-footed strike from outside of the area flew past Hornicek. Cracking goal, not much the goalkeeper could do about it.

Matthias Jaissle walks to the home dugout for the first time as manager. Just eight days until the proper stuff begins against Liverpool, a fixture which tends to throw up entertaining games. Bayer Leverkusen keep the home players waiting in the tunnel.

The former Liverpool defender has been linked with a move to Arsenal this week. Quansah is with his team-mates but not part of the matchday squad.

Bayer Leverkusen XI: Flekken; Gutierrez, Bade, Fernandez, Moreira, Tillman, Tapsoba, Arthur, Garcia, Maza, Kofane

Subs: Blaswich, Lomb, Hofmann, Terrier, Schick, Oermann, Tape, Poku, Vazquez, Boniface, Tella, Alfa-Ruprecht, Doganay, Hawighorst

Newcastle XI: Hornicek; M Miley, Thiaw (c), Botman, Hall; Steur, L Miley; Elanga, Woltemade, Barnes; Wissa

Subs: Harris, Charlton, Pivas, Sanusi, Johnson, Finneran, Neave

Today's team to take on Bayer Leverkusen in the @VisitMalta Weekender 👊 pic.twitter.com/ZfRvucBXSq

Newcastle United continue their preparations for the new season with a home friendly against Bayer Leverkusen, hoping to improve on their pretty limp showing against Everton at Murrayfield.

New manager ​Matthias Jaissle is ‌refusing to dwell on the departure of key players that has left his club in turmoil going into the Premier League season, insisting that he sees opportunity in the situation. Jaissle was recruited from Saudi Pro League side Al-Ahli after Eddie Howe left last month, with the German coach joining a club who had lost Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali and captain Bruno Guimaraes in quick succession.

“It’s a challenge, a big challenge, always when there’s a transitional period. ‌But it’s ‌not time to ⁠complain, it doesn’t make sense to see the negative things,” Jaissle said.

“We want to see the chance in that situation and that’s our approach from day one. We are here to do our ⁠best job. We want to support the players, the current squad.

“There will be adjustments to see in the coming days, weeks. But for now it’s only focused on the daily work, the work we can influence. That’s all that ​matters now.”

The 38-year-old coach arrived in Newcastle ‌having won two Austrian Bundesliga titles with Red Bull Salzburg before leading Al-Ahli to back-to-back AFC Champions League crowns.

He remained tight-lipped about new signings.

“Obviously, in that transition phase, the players who left the club were ‌great ​players, great characters, experienced ⁠players. This is now a vacuum,” he said.

“Either we adjust something in the squad, by signing these players, these profiles, or other players ⁠need to step up and fill ​these positions, these leadership roles. I’m quite optimistic, we can work in both scenarios.”

Jaissle said he had a ​clear vision of how he wants his team to play.

“The phrase how Newcastle ‌should play like is front-footed, intense, ​aggressive and of course also successful. ​In the end, it’s all about what ⁠I can ⁠say and it’s also why I’m sitting here,” he said.

“The approach we have as a coaching team and the identity of Newcastle is famed for, it’s so linked so close together - which is a perfect fit in my eyes and ​that’s going to be exciting.”

#2191. Ally McCoist left in stitches as Derek McInnes makes Rangers admission on-air

Rangers hero Ally McCoist was left in stitches as Derek McInnes issued an on-air one-liner over his start to life as Rangers manager.

The Ibrox hero couldn't contain his laughter as the Rangers boss admitted he faced a rocky opening to his tenure in Govan.

Rangers had exited the Europa League to Jagiellonia Bialystok, then the Conference League qualifiers to Jablonec before a draw and defeat in their opening two league matches.

However, since then Rangers have gone on a run of 11 matches unbeaten, advancing to the Premier Sports Cup final with victory over Aberdeen at Hampden this weekend.

But McInnes hasn't forgotten the early struggles as he joked with Jeff Stelling and McCoist on talkSPORT on Monday.

In a quip in response to Stelling's introduction discussing the challenges in the early stages of the season, McInnes said: "You've underestimated that slightly rocky part I think!"

The live stream then cut to McCoist who was doubled over at McInnes' honest assessment.

McInnes continued: "When you get a new job, it's normally for a reason – nothing is normally perfect. We had lots of work to do, but underneath it all, I felt if we came out the window with a strong enough squad, then we could compete. That's where we are at the minute.

"We needed a bit of confidence. The run started up at Aberdeen, going 11 games [unbeaten], and we're pleased with what we're doing. There's still a lot of improvement [needed]. But as Ally knows, at Rangers, we need to keep winning.

"The noise and everything that comes with it when you're not winning makes things so much more difficult.

"But I'm delighted with the response of the players. The game on Saturday was another case in point. We were the better team, we created more chances, we look as if we're scoring, but it took us too long to get the winning goal. But when it came, it was a great moment for us, and we look forward to the final now."

On there being progress to be made by his Rangers side, McInnes added: "There has to be (more improvement to come). No team is perfect at this stage of the season, the season is still in its infancy.

"People are so quick to judge and assume this is how it's going to be, but it's so early on. There's loads of improvements to come from us, but that's the same with most teams.

"We're a very young team, particularly in the forward line.

"A lot of stats will back that up. Sometimes we could do with a bit more nous and an older head up there just to try and make better decisions. But the potential is exciting, and the reach of some of these players is evident. But we need to try and win as we search for that potential."

#2190. A £4.7m West Brom transfer led James Morrison to an unexpected discovery

West Brom will be full of confidence following their heroics at West Ham last weekend, with a 3-1 victory on the road a statement win to boost their promotion credentials.

The Baggies lifted themselves up to fourth in the Championship standings after their Halloween treat at the London Stadium, with goals from Jimmy-Jay Morgan, Felix Horn Myhre and Callum Styles making it three wins from their last four league outings.

It’s been a remarkable turnaround ever since James Morrison stepped into the Baggies hotseat, and there’s so much positivity about where the club can go under his guidance.

One player who is beginning to flex his muscles in particular is goalscorer Myhre, who, despite a slow start in the blue and white stripes, is now beginning to show supporters how important his type of game is to the side.

But his move to The Hawthorns is an interesting story, with the transfer all coming about from the original scouting used to recruit Norwegian counterpart Aune Heggebo.

Felix Horn Myhre was part of 10 new recruits to walk through the West Brom building following a summer of change, with the Norwegian international one of many signings who was taking on the challenge of the Championship for the very first time.

And it’s safe to say that it’s taken a bit of time for the 27-year-old to get used to it, with boss James Morrison previously calling for patience with the midfielder as he gets used to the increase of physicality and intensity compared to his previous playing days with SK Brann.

And after 10 second tier games under his belt, Myhre is starting to show why Morrison was so keen to get him into the group for this season, with his tidiness on the ball and technical qualities bringing so much more composure in the final third, which has been needed for quite a long time.

Myhre has already been used in different positions so far in the early stages of the campaign, playing as either a central midfield, second striker or lone centre forward, with that kind of versatility so important over a gruelling Championship term.

As Myhre began life in the Championship, he was given starts immediately after signing, named in the starting XI for the first four games of the season, but the next five games would see him flip-flop between having a starting role to then being an unused substitute.

And while he was brought on late against Blackburn Rovers, he contributed immediately by grabbing his first goal for the club and sealing a 3-1 victory, with starts then coming once again against Preston North End and West Ham.

In those two games, Myhre’s performances have really gone up a notch, with the midfielder starting to link up effectively with the likes of Isaac Price and Jimmy-Jay Morgan, and that triangle of attack massively contributed to their destruction of West Ham last weekend.

Myhre’s goal at the London Stadium was an example of how the midfielder is getting into the right positions to score goals, while his layoff to Morgan for their second strike against the Hammers showed the technical quality he brings and composure when in tight and pressurised situations.

West Brom fans, are you starting to see the best of Felix Horn Myhre? How big of a player can he be for the Baggies this season? Comment below!

It’s so encouraging and brings excitement over what he can produce in the coming weeks and months, with Myhre having the potential to be one of the standout creative midfielders in the division if he keeps up his current form.

Meanwhile, an interesting story emerged from The Telegraph’s John Percy as to how West Brom ended up signing Felix Horn Myhre, with it all stemming from their capture the previous summer of Aune Heggebo.

Albion paid SK Brann a reported fee of £4.7m to sign Heggebo in the summer of 2025, with the frontman linking up under then Baggies boss Ryan Mason.

And James Morrison, who was working as part of the backroom staff at the time, watched Heggebo’s performances at Brann before the club went ahead with the transfer.

During the scouting, he was left impressed with the displays of Myhre, who was also playing for SK Brann at the time, but Brann reportedly refused to sell Myhre and Heggebo together in the same window given they were such important players.

Because of that, Albion had to wait until the summer just gone to see Myhre eventually join the club when Morrison had his full say on transfers, with the midfielder signing for an initial £2.5m fee, rising to £3.1m.

It’s amazing how one piece of transfer business can have a much wider impact than first expected, with West Brom never likely to even have considered Felix Horn Myhre as a target if they hadn’t scouted Aune Heggebo in the first place.

And due to that piece of recruitment, Albion have landed themselves on a gem of a midfield player, who is finding his feet and showing a technical side to his game that is reminiscent of the likes of Robert Koren, who was such a wonderful player for the Baggies both at Championship level and then stepping up to be an accomplished Premier League asset.

Myhre's influence is now beginning to grow ten-fold, as demonstrated by his glittering performance at West Ham, and all connected with Albion will be hoping those types of displays can continue and help the Baggies cement themselves towards the top end of the table.

This kind of signing could be so key to Albion being true promotion contenders this season, albeit being such an unexpected discovery in the summer of 2025.

#2189. Ally McCoist reveals vital Rangers transfer advice for star man Olwethu Makhanya

Ally McCoist reckons Olwethu Makhanya should have no thoughts of leaving Rangers any time soon despite attracting attention with his outstanding start to life at Ibrox.

The South African defender has emerged as one of the club's standout performers since arriving from Philadelphia Union in a £3million deal. Comfortable at centre-back and capable of covering on the left side of defence, Makhanya has become a key figure in Derek McInnes' plans.

His impressive form has inevitably sparked talk of interest from elsewhere, but Rangers legend McCoist believes the 22-year-old is in the ideal place to continue his development and establish himself further.

Speaking to talkSPORT Bet Online Casino, McCoist said: "Pat Nevin generally talks an awful lot of sense, and he's spot on here. I don't think Makhanya should be in any rush to go anywhere.

Read more: Thelo Aasgaard receives glowing 'DNA' praise on Rangers loan exit

"He's had a very good start, though the weekend was maybe a little reminder that you don't get any easy games and you're a target.

"So, from that point of view, there's no doubt that with the way he's started, there will be clubs looking at him.

"But I would be advising him to stay for a while, get the job done, keep getting rave reports, and see where it takes him."

McCoist is also encouraged by the progress Rangers have made under McInnes and insists the club's ambitions should remain as high as ever despite their European disappointment.

The former striker believes domestic success must be the priority, with the Premiership title remaining the ultimate target.

He added: "I don't think anything has changed. I think Rangers have got to set out right now to win every domestic trophy they can.

"You have to be looking to win the league title, that is the most important one at the start of the season for a team like Rangers.

"The Cups I always say are a more than achievable bonus, but you've got to get the league title.

"That is still the priority for me looking at it, and the priority for most Rangers fans right now."

The former Stockport County boss has officially taken charge at Hillsborough in place of Henrik Pedersen, and has agreed to a contract until June 2030, with Antony Sweeney and Clint Hill also taking on roles in his backroom staff.

Pedersen oversaw a busy summer transfer window alongside new sporting director Simon Wilson, with as many as 18 players joining the club.

The pair worked together at Stockport, where the coach led the team to consecutive play-off place finishes in League One before departing last summer, and the sporting director has highlighted his talents from their time together at the Hatters.

"Dave was the outstanding candidate following a detailed and comprehensive recruitment process, and we're delighted to welcome him to Sheffield Wednesday,” said Wilson, via the club’s website.

The 51-year-old took over at Stockport on 2 November 2021, exactly five years before being appointed by the Owls, and he guided the team to promotion twice during his spell in charge.

Sheffield Wednesday fans are pleased with the new owners’ approach to the head coach appointment, claiming there is a newfound level of professionalism behind the scenes.

Others have noticed that Challinor has been given the title of manager, rather than head coach, which bucks the recent trend in English football.

The former Stockport manager’s arrival has been likened to Tiger Woods approaching the back nine in his famous Sunday red polo.

Ultimately, fans are optimistic that Challinor is the right appointment for Sheffield Wednesday.

The new manager’s first game in charge will come away to Oldham Athletic on 8 November in a 5.15pm kick-off.

Challinor’s style of football isn’t the easiest on the eye all the time, but it’s proven quite effective at a League One level with Stockport.

His track record is impressive, and his previous working relationship with Wilson is a good base to start with at Hillsborough.

It’s no surprise that they’ve linked up together again given the success they enjoyed at their previous club, and Arise Capital will now be hoping they can enjoy similar success between now and June 2030.

A long-term contract is a big vote of confidence for Challinor, and shows he will be given time to make things work at Hillsborough, although he will be under pressure to achieve promotion sooner rather than later.

#2186. Edson Alvarez & ex-West Ham teammates react as Nuno is sacked

Edson Alvarez has liked a post confirming that Nuno Espírito Santo had been sacked as West Ham United manager.

The Hammers were widely expected to push for the Championship title this season, but, even though they are only six points away from top spot, they have had an inconsistent start to the campaign.

A disappointing 3-1 reverse at home to West Brom on Saturday meant the Irons had suffered back-to-back home defeats, and it left the Londoners sitting 8th in the Championship.

Therefore, the pressure was building on the manager, and it was announced on Tuesday morning that the former Wolves chief had been dismissed.

Interestingly, the post shared by West Ham on Instagram also prompted responses by both current and former players.

Alvarez, who has been frozen out by Nuno this season, with the Mexican international yet to play a minute for the club in the league, was seen to be liking the update.

Elsewhere, George Earthy and Callum Wilson were two former players to like the message from the club confirming Nuno’s exit.

Wilson was released on a free this summer after a difficult relationship with Nuno last season, with the boss having been ready to sanction his exit ahead of the January window before then calling on the experienced striker.

West Ham United have parted company with Portuguese head coach Nuno Espirito Santo and set their sights on Scott Parker

Meanwhile, Earthy may have hoped for a chance with his boyhood club this season following relegation, but he was sold to Reading on a permanent basis in the summer.

Of course, we don’t know the exact details of what has gone on between Alvarez and Nuno, but there’s no denying that midfield is a major issue for the team.

They are lacking a physical, defensive midfielder that would provide balance to the XI, and it’s a key reason as to why they have shipped far too many goals.

So, fans were naturally wondering why Alvarez, and Soungoutou Magassa, were not playing under Nuno, and it's something that Scott Parker, who is poised to take over, will surely look to rectify immediately.

Even if the duo wanted to leave in the summer, which seems likely, the reality is that once the window had closed, it would make sense for all parties to come together to ensure they could contribute - until January at least.

This gives an insight into the division that may have existed at West Ham under Nuno’s guidance, and it did show at times on the pitch.

Obviously, last season was very tough, but, to their credit, the Hammers did put up a fight to stay in the league after a disappointing start to the campaign.

But, this season was always going to be different. West Ham are the big fish in the Championship, and the resources they boast means anything other than promotion is a failure.

Are West Ham right to sack Nuno Espírito Santo for Scott Parker? Let us know in the comments below.

With that in mind, Nuno can have few complaints about losing his job considering the team are occupying the final play-off place going into the midweek games.

As well as that, the performances have been alarming, and it will now be down to Parker to try and unite the dressing room to help West Ham go on a run to close that gap to the top two.

#2185. Ally McCoist in public Rangers transfer plea to star man - don't go anywhere yet

Ally McCoist believes Olwethu Makhanya should stay at Rangers, despite his impressive start earning acclaim.

The South African defender has become a key player for the club since his £3 million move from Philadelphia Union.

He has impressed at both centre-back and the left side of defence, making him a vital part of Derek McInnes' plans.

His form will likely catch the eye of other clubs, but Rangers legend McCoist thinks the 22-year-old should stay put and continue his development at Ibrox.

Speaking to talkSPORT Bet Online Casino, McCoist said: "Pat Nevin generally talks an awful lot of sense, and he's spot on here.]

Read more: Celtic handed fresh agony as star who got away rewrites Eredivisie record books

"I don't think Makhanya should be in any rush to go anywhere."

He acknowledged Makhanya's strong start but reminded him that the weekend's performance was a reminder that there are no easy games and he is a target.

"From that point of view, there's no doubt that with the way he's started, there will be clubs looking at him.

"But I would be advising him to stay for a while, get the job done, keep getting rave reports, and see where it takes him."

McCoist is also positive about Rangers' progress under McInnes and believes the club's ambitions should remain high, despite European disappointments.

The former striker emphasised the importance of domestic success, with the Premiership title being the ultimate goal.

He said: "I don't think anything has changed.

"I think Rangers have got to set out right now to win every domestic trophy they can.

"You have to be looking to win the league title, that is the most important one at the start of the season for a team like Rangers.

"The Cups I always say are a more than achievable bonus, but you've got to get the league title."

McCoist concluded that while Makhanya's value may be increasing, Rangers is the ideal platform for him to continue building his reputation before considering a move.

#2184. Rashford returns and Fernandes misses another penalty as Man Utd humbled by Amorim

Bruno Fernandes missed a penalty for the second successive pre-season friendly as Manchester United were beaten 4-2 by former head coach Ruben Amorim’s AC Milan.

Fernandes, who rolled a spot-kick wide in a shoot-out against Leeds in midweek, was gifted the chance to open his pre-season account in Wroclaw, Poland.

His effort was on target this time, but Milan keeper Lorenzo Torriani dived to his right to beat the shot away.

Fernandes did at least get an assist, taking the second-minute corner which was powerfully headed home by Harry Maguire to give United the lead.

Amorim’s Milan equalised after a defensive mix-up allowed Gonçalo Ramos to break into the area and square for Samuel Chukwueze to roll home.

United were awarded their penalty just before half-time after Koni De Winter tugged back Youri Tielemans, but Torriani guessed correctly to leave Fernandes frustrated.

United retook the lead after Patrick Dorgu pounced on a loose backpass from Filippo Terracciano, but Milan equalised again when Chukwueze’s wayward shot was poked in by Alphadjo Cissè at the far post.

Marcus Rashford, who was frozen out by Amorim and loaned out to Aston Villa and then Barcelona, came on as a substitute on the hour for his first United appearance since returning from Spain.

But Milan went ahead in the 68th minute when Chukwueze’s cross was headed home by Ramos, and three minutes later former Chelsea midfielder Ruben Loftus-Cheek raced through to hit the fourth and cap a performance that underlines United’s need for reinforcements before their season starts in earnest next Saturday, away at Hull City.

Manchester United (4-2-3-1) Lammens; Mazraoui (Dalot 61), Maguire, Heaven (Martinez 61), Shaw; Tielemans, Santos (Mainoo 61); Diallo (Lacey 61), Fernandes, Dorgu (Rashford 61); Cunha (Mbeumo 61). Subs Zirkzee, Yoro, J Fletcher, T Fletcher, Amass, Collyer, Mee (g), Heath (g), Gabriel. Booked Dorgu.

AC Milan (3-4-2-1) Torriani; Terracciano (Gila 60), Winter (Vladimirov 84), Pavlovic (Diawara 84); Chukwueze, Musah (Ricci 76), Jashari (Modric 60), Estupinan (Bartesaghi 61); Loftus-Cheek (Comotto 84), Cisse (Saelemaekers 60); Ramos (Camarda 75). Subs Pittarella (g), Bouyer (g). Booked Estupinan.

Goals Chukwueze (37), Cisse (57), Ramos (68), Loftus-Cheek (71).

That six-time Champions League winner Luka Modric raised the trophy with the one hand said everything you need to know about this moment...

Aug 30: Manchester United vs Ipswich Town

Sep 13: Manchester United vs Manchester City

United’s pre-season ends in defeat. A wretched second half proves their undoing as Amorim’s Milan score four. Worth reminding that United led this match, twice.

Milan are playing keep-ball in these latter stages and although Mainoo regains possession, his attempt to play forward is cut out and Modric’s outside-of-the-foot pass finds Comotto, who heads straight at Lammens.

Four minutes of added time to be played...

United now raining crosses down on Milan’s box but Torriani equal to it every time.

For the second time this afternoon, Shaw directs a lovely ball into Fernandes’ path in behind Milan’s back line, but the Portugal international can’t bring it under his spell.

Martinez has added a little bit of urgency to United’s build-up. Mbeumo tries to feed Shaw down the line but the ball is cut out.

More substitutions... Diawara, Vladimirov and Comotto enter the field of play in place of Pavlovic, De Winter and Loftus-Cheek.

Big chance for Rashford! Martinez lofts a fantastic ball over the top but Rashford is not quite able to bring it under his spell, with Torriani and De Winter combing to clear their lines.

Milan are now sitting off, settling into a back five as they look to preserve their advantage. Fernandes, Tielemans and Dalot combine well but such has been United’s fortunes this afternoon, the ball ricochets off the referee and play is halted.

Good work from Rashford in the corner to regain possession, but his ball into the box is not picked up by a team-mate.

More changes... Ramos and Musah make way for Camarda and Ricci.

Manchester United 2 AC Milan 4 (Loftus-Cheek) No sooner had the players returned after the second-half hydration break then Milan exploit United’s exposed left side (again). Ramos sends Loftus-Cheek through and the midfielder composes himself before bending the ball around Lammens.

Manchester United 2 AC Milan 3 (Ramos) That’s too easy. United fail to learn their lesson, Shaw not getting tight enough to Chukwueze and the winger’s cross is met by new signing Ramos, who powers a header back across goal and past Lammens.

Loftus-Cheek and Ramos are doing a good job of cutting off the pass into United’s midfield in their build-up phase.

Rashford (who makes his first United appearance in almost two years), Lacey, Dalot, Mbeumo, Mainoo and Martinez replace Dorgu, Amad, Mazraoui, Cunha, Santos and Heaven.

For Milan, Saelemaekers, Bartesaghi, Gila and Modric are on for Cisse, Estupinan, Terracciano and Jashari

Manchester United 2 AC Milan 2 (Cisse) United have set a higher defensive line so far this half, with their front line pressing with more intensity to avoid the ball over the top. However Chukwueze is able to find space around the sides, coming in off the right and curling an effort goalwards which Cisse turns in at the far post. There are calls for offside, but with no VAR here, the goal stands.

Milan win a free-kick some 25 yards out after Fernandes clips Estupinan. Teenager Cisse steps up and fires straight into the United wall. Was always going to be difficult to trouble Lammens from there.

Manchester United 2 AC Milan 1 (Dorgu) United wisely decide to keep hold of the ball for a while, the midfield three rotating to disrupt Milan’s out-of-possession shape and open up passing lanes. A Milan throw-in from the right-back berth is precedes an awful backpass by Terracciano which is pounced on by Dorgu who curls the ball beyond Torriani.

United have looked bright in the opening moments of this half. They win a free-kick midway into Milan’s half. The ball is delivered to the back post and, after some 18-yard-box pinball, a relieved Torriano pounces on it.

Both teams remain unchanged as the second 45 minutes begin.

All square at the break. Tough to know what to make of that half – United looked solid enough and could have taken a lead into the interval had Fernandes converted his penalty, but they failed to create a wealth of clear-cut chances. It will be interesting to see how Carrick approaches this second half.

Milan have enjoyed just a tick over two-thirds of possession, which United have contributed to in part through some lackadaisical passing.

Fernandes misses a spot-kick for the second time in two friendlies! Here, Torriani guesses correctly, diving to his right to palm Fernandes’ strike away.

De Winter brings down Tielemans inside the box after Terracciano loses the ball attempting to play out from the back.

Manchester United 1 AC Milan 1 (Chukwueze) It’s all a bit messy. Jashari causes Maguire and Santos to crash into each other (Kaka at Old Trafford, anyone?) off a throw-in, Ramos taking over with the United pair out of commission. He finds Chukwueze who finishes the move off at the far post.

The match becomes stretched momentarily as Pavlovic, the centre-back, marauds forward, setting the ball to Estupinan who delivers another dangerous cross from the left, which Lammens does well to claim.

Santos clips Loftus-Cheek near the byline and the referee awards Milan a free-kick. Chukwueze cuts the ball back to an unmarked Jashari on the edge of the box, but his side-footed effort flies wide.

Milan supporters unfurl a banner paying tribute to the late, great Franco Baresi, who passed away on July 31 aged 66.

Hermosa bandera a Franco Baresi.QUE EN PAZ DESCANSE, LEYENDA DEL FÚTBOL 🙏🏻 pic.twitter.com/fvE48nKVSs

United have picked their moments to press. Santos, who has enjoyed a wonderful pre-season, is a little too overzealous in his attempts to regain possession and gives away a foul. But the intent is correct.

Shaw floats a delightful ball over the top for Fernandes to gallop on to. The Portuguese steals in ahead of De Winter but cannot find the target with his weaker left foot.

Cisse escapes the clutches of Mazraoui down the left and fires a shot (more likely a mis-hit cross) straight into the gloves of Lammens.

United finally get their foot on the ball, but Heaven attempts an ambitious cross-field pass and possession goes back to the Italians.

A Mexican wave has already begun. We’re only 21 minutes in...

Carrick’s side continue to sit off, allowing Milan to keep hold of the ball. Cisse works in from the left, playing a neat one-two with Ramos before his curled strike sails well over.

A period of extended possession for Milan, United dropping into a compact 4-4-2 mid-block. Estupinan rains in a dangerous cross from the left and the ball falls to Loftus-Cheek, whose effort is expertly saved by the right boot of Lammens.

Estupinan goes into the book after pulling Amad’s shirt as he looked to dart in behind after Tielemans had played a dangerous through-ball. Might possibly have been the last man?

Tielemans cedes possession to the busy Jashari just outside his own box, the Swiss midfielder moving the ball on to Loftus-Cheek who fires a shot straight at Lammens.

Amad picks Pavlovic’s pocket and the Milan centre-half is forced to concede a corner. United unable to score from this one.

Milan are indeed in Amorim’s preferred 3-4-2-1 formation. They circulate the ball in front of United’s first line of pressure in an attempt to calm things down.

Manchester United 1 AC Milan 0 (Maguire) Fernandes delivers an inswinger from the left and Maguire is there to meet it at the back post, striding past Musa to plant a header past Torriani.

United make a fast start, Dorgu flashing a cross-cum-shot across the face of goal. Torriani gets a fingertip to it and thte ball goes behind for a corner.

Szymon Marciniak, the experienced Polish referee, gets us under way. Milan send the ball back to goalkeeper Torriani.

The players emerge from the tunnel, United debuting their lovely new cream third kit and Milan in their traditional red-and-black home colours. Smoke machines and pyrotechnics add to the atmosphere in Wroclaw...

We are almost ready to go. Let us know your match predictions and thoughts on United’s prospects this season in the comments section beneath this blog.

Manchester United defeated Leeds United on penalties to hoist the mighty Boyle Sports Cup at Croke Park. The match, a 1-1 draw, was brought to an abrupt end after five young pitch invaders ran to the middle of the field to take selfies with Bruno Fernandes. In the shoot-out it was James Justin who missed the “decisive” spot-kick, paving the way for Noussair Mazraoui to win it for United.

Marcus Rashford is on the bench this afternoon and could make his first United appearance since his cameo in a Europa League win over Viktoria Plzen in December 2024. He was frozen out under Amorim and has since been loaned to Aston Villa and Barcelona, but his Old Trafford future under Carrick remains unclear.

Michael Carrick believes Manchester United can push for the Premier League title, but has underlined the urgent need for signings.

The United head coach has taken heart from his squad’s promising preparations for the new campaign and, speaking at their Co Kildare summer base, he explained why he was confident they could build on last season’s third-place finish.

Carrick has been thrilled to hear United’s players discussing what they might achieve and has dared supporters to dream that they can get closer to last year’s champions Arsenal. But he is also a realist and recognises he is not blessed with options.

So far United have added Youri Tielemans, Andrey Santos and Karl Darlow, a reserve goalkeeper, but their £83.3m spend is significantly less than what newly promoted clubs Ipswich Town (£109.4m) and Coventry City (£92.2m) have invested in their squads.

Amorim’s side have gone intercontinental this summer, travelling from Scotland to Indonesia, via Australia, before arriving in Poland for the last of their four pre-season games.

In memory of Franco Baresi 🇮🇹♾️ pic.twitter.com/ULAJRjxDvE

Manchester United Lammens; Mazraoui, Maguire, Heaven, Shaw; Tielemans, Santos, Fernandes; Amad, Dorgu; Cunha

Subs Heath, Mee, Amass, Dalot, Martínez, Yoro, Collyer, J. Fletcher, T. Fletcher, Mainoo, Gabriel, Lacey, Mbeumo, Rashford, Zirkzee

AC Milan Torriani; Terracciano, De Winter, Pavlović; Chukwueze, Jashari, Musah, Estupiñán; Loftus-Cheek, Cissè; Ramos

Subs Bouyer, Pittarella, Gila, Diawara, Vladimirov, Ricci, Saelemaekers, Bartesaghi, Modrić, Comotto, Camarda

At his AC Milan unveiling, Amorim was asked about the learnings from his United tenure that he would take into his new role. He said: “The first thing is it’s hard to explain the mistakes because for that I would have to explain the context of the last adventure.

“It’s hard to say to you every mistake. The only thing I can say is that I learned a lot and I made some mistakes.

“I didn’t have the opportunity, and I’m sorry for that, I didn’t have the opportunity to say something to the Manchester United fans at the moment and I’m really proud to be their coach for a year in that time.

“But now it’s a different history. There are a lot of things that I could do better in the last experience but sometimes it’s like that, you need to learn to find the right spot to reach a different level and that’s my thinking here.

“Everyone learns from their experience. I learned a lot, I did some mistakes I will try to change, there are some thing you will never change but I think I will be a better manager, that’s all.”

Welcome to live coverage of Manchester United’s final pre-season match, against AC Milan in Wroclaw, Poland. Michael Carrick’s side will look to apply the finishing touches to a promising summer on the pitch, which has included victories over Rosenborg and Atlético Madrid, plus a draw against European champions Paris St-Germain. The team will fly back to Manchester with the big ones, the ones they have always wanted – the Snapdragon Cup and the Boyle Sports Cup – in tow.

At the Tarczynski Stadium there will be a reunion with former manager Ruben Amorim, who was appointed AC Milan’s head coach in June, five months after being sacked by United. Following a frustrating season under Massimiliano Allegri in which Milan fell out of the Champions League spots on the final day, the Rossoneri said Amorim would bring a “modern dominant tactical approach”. His methods failed to cut through at Old Trafford, though, during a tumultuous 14-month reign which finally ended after the Portuguese “blew up” during a heated meeting with director of football Jason Wilcox. At Milan, Amorim has persisted with the 3-4-2-1 formation that was doomed at United.

Carrick made clear this week that United must strengthen if they are to challenge for titles. So far the club have brought in Youri Tielemans, Andrey Santos and Karl Darlow, but they are still in the market for a left-back and another midfielder. The future of Marcus Rashford has also been a topic of conversation among United fans. The forward has not played for his boyhood club since December 2024 but has joined up with his team-mates in Poland and it remains to be seen if he features in Carrick’s forward planning.

Kobbie Mainoo, who did not play a minute at this summer’s World Cup, and Lisandro Martínez have also joined up with the team this week and could be handed their first minutes of pre-season having been named in the matchday squad. For Milan, new signing Gonçalo Ramos – bought from PSG for £63m – will make his first appearance in the famous red and black.

#2183. Manchester United confirmed lineup: Amad & Yoro return to starting lineup

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

Manchester United and Tottenham Hotspur return from the international break with plenty to prove when they meet at Old Trafford on Saturday.

Michael Carrick’s side have won just once in their last four domestic matches since beating Ipswich 5-2. A Carabao Cup defeat to Brighton was followed by a loss to 10-man Manchester City, before Manchester United drew with Everton and Fulham. Matheus Cunha’s late equaliser at Fulham rescued a point, but Manchester United still sit 12th.

Roberto De Zerbi’s side are bottom of the Premier League with only two points from their opening five games. Spurs have failed to score in four of those matches, while defeats against Aston Villa and Newcastle have added to the pressure.

Michael Carrick has named his starting eleven for the clash at Old Trafford, with Kobbie Mainoo and Youri Tielemans partnering in midfield as United look to get their season back on track.

Senne Lammens starts in goal, with Leny Yoro, Lisandro Martinez, Harry Maguire and Luke Shaw forming the back four. Carrick has opted for Mainoo and Tielemans in the middle, with Amad Diallo, Bruno Fernandes and Matheus Cunha tasked with supporting Bryan Mbeumo up front.

Leny Yoro had a brilliant international break where he made his debut for France. His performance on debut was enough for Zidane to praise the debutant.

Amad, after missing the start of the season with an injury, returns straightaway to the team.

Carlos Baleba starts on the bench and is expected to make his debut today. Marcus Rashford is also on the bench alongside Shea Lacey.

Lammens; Yoro, Martinez, Maguire, Shaw; Mainoo, Tielemans; Amad, Bruno Fernandes, Mbeumo; Cunha.

Mbeumo gets his place through the middle, while Amad and Cunha start on the wing after scoring the late equaliser against Fulham. Fernandes will be expected to start producing the numbers from last season after a lackluster start to the season, except against Ipswich, before the international break.

United need a response after a difficult run, but Tottenham arrive under pressure of their own. With both sides desperate for points, the starting lineups set the stage for an important afternoon at Old Trafford.
