#2028. Man City to accept Rayan Ait-Nouri offer ahead of January - transfer expert

Manchester City are prepared to accept offers for Rayan Ait-Nouri ahead of the upcoming January transfer window.

The 25-year-old has struggled to nail down a place in Enzo Maresca's side so far this season, despite impressing when called upon, and is unlikely to be part of his long-term plans.

A number of Premier League clubs and others across Europe are believed to be keeping a close eye on his situation and would now be prepared to lure him away from the Etihad.

Former Man United chief scout Mick Brown told Football Insider that Maresca "doesn't rate" Ait-Nouri and will facilitate his exit if the right offer arrives in the mid-season window.

The Algeria international has yet to make a Premeir League appearance this season, while his minutes across other competitions have also been limited.

There is plenty of competition for places at left-back in this Man City side, with Josko Gvardiol and Nico O'Reilly in the way, opening the door for Ait-Nouri to move on.

Football Insider revealed in September that Maresca had plans to utlilise Ait-Nouri as part of his squad after his impressive performances in the Champions League this season.

However, his lack of playing time in the Premier League has raised new questions about his future, and there is a growing feeling he could be allowed to leave.

With a number of clubs keeping a close eye on his situation, Ait-Nouri is expected to seek a move away from Man City in January, with both the club and the player ready to move on.

"It doesn't seem like there is any place for Rayan Ait-Nouri in this Man City team," Brown told Football Insider.

"Look at their usual left-backs, you've got Gvardiol and O'Reilly, which one of those two would you leave out to put Ait-Nouri in? Realistically, that's not going to happen.

"He might get minutes here and there off the bench or in cup games, but it's become clear already this season that he isn't trusted to play in the Premier League.

"It seems to me that Enzo Maresca doesn't rate him, he doesn't see him as a big part of his squad, and he would be ready to let him go in January.

"From the player's point of view, I expect he'll be ready to move on as well, because if he's not playing regularly in this City team then he will want to go and play somewhere else.

"I can't see him staying at Man City for much longer, it's clear he doesn't have a real part to play, so it's probably best for everybody if he leaves."

Despite his lack of playing time at Man City in recent seasons, Ait-Nouri still remains very highly regarded by a number of Premier League clubs who could lure him away.

Everton and Tottenham have both been long-term admirers, while clubs outside of English football including the likes of AC Milan and Juventus are also very keen.

Meanwhile, Football Insider revealed in September that Man United saw a deadline-day move for Ait-Nouri blocked by Man City as they didn't want to see him join a rival club.

That move could be reignited in January, however, with United still among his high-profile admirers and Man City believed to be more open to his departure.

Michael Carrick is determined to add a new left-back to his squad, and while a deal for Ait-Nouri may only be a loan for now, he remains high on Man United's list.

#2026. Oliver Glasner tipped to 'go back to Crystal Palace' after leaving Nottingham Forest - expert

Oliver Glasner could well return to Crystal Palace if he is sacked at Nottingham Forest.

That is the opinion of experienced former Aston Villa, Tottenham and Everton scout, Bryan King, speaking exclusively to Football Insider.

The Austrian only left the Eagles in the summer after seeing out the end of his contract, having enjoyed a hugely successful two years at Selhurst Park.

Glasner was replaced by Pierre Sage, who now appears to be on the brink of departure following just two Premier League wins from the opening nine games of the season.

Nottingham Forest have won just one, with Glasner at significant risk if his side cannot produce a positive result in their final game before the international break.

The Tricky Trees will welcome Manchester City to the City Ground on Saturday, looking to take advantage of a slight blip for Enzo Maresca's team.

The relationship between Glasner and Palace chairman Steve Parish had become exceedingly toxic mid-way through last season.

The Austrian felt that his squad had been abandoned, and made it clear that he would not renew his contract.

With his team on a terrible run of form, Palace considered sacking Glasner before both sides ultimately agreed to end the season amicably, leading to Conference League glory.

"They're a side that are struggling at the moment, Palace", King told Football Insider. "And without any doubt, the coach now must be under pressure.

"If you're talking about [Michael] Carrick and Glasner at Nottingham Forest. There you go - if he gets a sack at Nottingham Forest, he'll go back to Palace.

"The only way he went to Nottingham Forest is because of the money that was on offer. There's no other sane way to go and work for a bloke like that owner, because you know what's going to come. You lose three matches and you're in trouble."

Even after the international break, things do not get easier for Nottingham Forest.

Bournemouth and Chelsea will be up first before a trip to Hull City and the visit of Brighton.

Glasner will be lucky to still have his job by that stage, however. "It's now time not to make compromises, it's now time to show a clear way and everybody has to follow," he said following Saturday's defeat to Brentford.

"And if they don't want to follow, then I guess then the sixth manager will come in."

Club statement. Read more: https://t.co/LT0TZXbSpR https://t.co/0r6Yz55iRi

— West Ham United (@WestHam) November 3, 2026

But West Ham have now decided to make a change following back-to-back home defeats, leaving the club eighth in the Championship.

Saturday’s 3-1 loss to West Brom prompted what the Hammers described as a “thorough review” of their start to life in the second tier.

The club had opted to stick with Nuno in May despite his failure to preserve their Premier League status, but the Portuguese coach has now been removed from his position.

The managerial change provides an intriguing twist for Arne Engels, who only left Celtic for West Ham in August.

The Belgian made the move in a £22m deal after Celtic rejected two earlier bids, with Martin O’Neill admitting at the time that Engels wanted the transfer and did not want to risk injury by playing in the Hoops’ Champions League play-off.

Martin O’Neill also described the midfielder’s departure as “disappointing” and conceded his running power would be difficult for Celtic to replace.

The ‘biggest trick’ Celtic missed that could come back to haunt them

Rangers-daft pundit sounds Celtic alarm with ‘Covid year’ warning

Celtic's tactics under Martin O'Neill torn apart as ‘biggest pet hate’ laid bare

Arne Engels has since been a regular under Nuno, starting every league match following his arrival, but will now have to impress whoever takes charge next.

West Ham said: “West Ham United can confirm that men’s first-team head coach Nuno Espírito Santo has left his position with immediate effect.

“Following a thorough review of the start to the EFL Championship season, the board of directors believe that a change is necessary at this time in order to ensure that the club’s objectives and expectations remain on track.

“Assistant head coach Rui Pedro Silva and goalkeeper coach Rui Barbosa have also departed.

“West Ham United would like to thank Nuno, Rui and Rui for their hard work and commitment during their time at the club, and wish them all the very best for the future.

“The process of recruiting a new head coach is already underway.”

Mark Noble, Steve Potts and Gerard Prenderville will take temporary charge of preparations for Wednesday night’s Championship trip to Cardiff City.

#2018. Bundesliga top scorer Füllkrug reflects positively on Milan spell: “A truly wonderful time”

Niclas Füllkrug has reflected on his short time with AC Milan, admitting he would have liked to have made more of a mark.

Füllkrug is enjoying a stellar start to the season with Werder Bremen, with 11 goals in nine games across the Bundesliga and DFB-Pokal, the last of which came on Tuesday with a brace in the cup against his former team, Borussia Dortmund.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

The second goal was one of the finest of his career and these staggering numbers put him ahead of some of the great strikers of recent years, including Ballon d’Or winner Harry Kane who has 10 goals for Bayern Munich this season.

It has been a fruitful return to Bremen so far, and as a result the German striker is once again being talked about a possible return to the national team under Jurgen Klopp. He spoke to MilanNews journalist Alessandro Schiavone.

Eleven goals already, and we’re not even in November, after your return to Werder Bremen. Could you have scored more with Milan?

“Yes, of course. It’s a new season now, but I could have scored a few more goals and provided a few more assists at AC Milan, too.

“It was a bit of an unlucky period, and not the most effective in terms of goalscoring, but I still think I put in several good performances. It was a truly, truly wonderful time, and I still have great affection for AC Milan.”

Your winning goal against Lecce was a typical Füllkrug goal. What’s it like scoring at San Siro? Is it comparable to scoring at Signal Iduna Park in Dortmund?

“Yes, it’s quite similar to Dortmund. In Dortmund it’s a little different, there are still a few more people. But San Siro is amazing! It’s a historic stadium, special and truly, truly wonderful.”

“It’s difficult, difficult! Ultimately, the decision isn’t down to just one person. There were West Ham and AC Milan. There have been many changes at the top of AC Milan, and so…

“I still follow AC Milan, I watch the games, and I’m still in touch with some of the players and the lads. I wish them all the best. My best friend at AC Milan? Ardon Jashari.”

Milan could have kept you for just €5m, but was it the club that told you they didn’t want to keep you, or did you find out through the media?

“I can’t say anything about that… absolutely nothing (smiles).”

And what about the Champions League failure?

“I’d rather not say anything about that, too, because I don’t know. And then it would be too much…”

AC Milan are having an up-and-down season. Are you still following them?

“When I can, I watch the games. I still have some friends there I’m in touch with. I wish AC Milan all the best.”

#2015. Hearts pay tribute as former captain Don Murray dies aged 80

Former Heart of Midlothian captain Don Murray has died at the age of 80.

The central defender spent almost two years at Tynecastle during the 1970s and captained the Jambos during the inaugural Scottish Premier Division season.

It is with great sadness to announce the passing of former captain, Don Murray, at the age of 80. An iron-hard central defender, Don spent less than two years at Tynecastle, but he made a fine contribution, assisting Hearts to qualify for the initial Scottish Premier Division campaign, as well as reaching the Scottish Cup Final in May 1976. Our thoughts are with Don's family and friends at this time ♥️ A tribute to Don, by Club Historian, David Speed, can be read on our website 👉 https://t.co/2FJZwVWGfT

— Heart of Midlothian FC (@JamTarts) November 3, 2026

Hearts announced that Murray died on Monday at Llandough, near Cardiff, and paid tribute to a player who made 71 appearances for the club.

The club said: “It is with great sadness that the club learned on Monday of the death of former captain, Don Murray, at Llandough, near Cardiff. He was 80 years of age.”

Born into a farming family at Duffus, near Elgin, in January 1946, Murray began playing with Hopeman Junior School before progressing to junior football with Burghead Thistle.

He signed for Cardiff City in January 1963 and went on to become an influential figure at the Welsh club.

Murray made 527 appearances for Cardiff and helped them reach the League Cup semi-finals during the 1965-66 season and the European Cup Winners’ Cup semi-finals two years later.

His performances also earned international recognition with Scotland at under-23 level.

After a brief loan spell at Swansea City, Murray joined Hearts for £15,000 in December 1974.

Don Murray (Image: Colorsport / Shutterstock)

His arrival helped bring stability to a difficult campaign as Hearts secured their place in the newly formed Premier Division for the following season.

Murray was subsequently appointed captain and led the Jambos during that historic first Premier Division campaign, when they finished fifth.

Hearts also reached the Scottish Cup final in 1976, although Murray was denied the opportunity to lead the team out against Rangers at Hampden because of a calf injury.

He remained captain for the club’s subsequent tour of Norway and Australasia, but continued to struggle with the injury at the beginning of the following season.

Murray left Hearts for Newport County in October 1976 after making 71 appearances for the Edinburgh club and later played for Barry Town.

Following his retirement from football, Murray worked as a social worker.

Hearts added: “Don always led by example.”

The club extended its condolences to Murray’s family and friends following his death.

#2012. GdS: ‘Crazy desire’ – why Amorim hopes Cisse can become the derby hero

Alphadjo Cisse has had an electric start to the season so far with AC Milan, and Ruben Amorim could turn to him in the hopes of derby heroics.

La Gazzetta dello Sport (seen below) recall that during Wednesday’s defeat to Bologna at San Siro, the crowd chanted Cisse’s name louder than any other Milan player’s, even before a game that truly cemented his status as the player of the moment.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

He will remain the team’s top scorer for the time being, unless Adrien Rabiot nets a hat-trick in the derby, or Goncalo Ramos or Diego Moreira pull off a four-goal haul. As it stands, Cisse leads the way with seven goals, followed by Adrien with four.

Cisse’s goals are fairly evenly split: four in the league and three in the Europa League. In Serie A, he reached this tally in 338 minutes of play, while in Salzburg, he needed just 207 minutes to record his first Rossoneri hat-trick.

His scoring rate is exceptionally high: one goal every 84.5 minutes in the league, a figure that improves to one every 69 minutes in international competition. And to those who might argue that many of these goals came from lucky, close-range touches, others are not scoring goals like that.

On his own, he has accounted for a third of the 21 total goals scored by Ruben Amorim’s side, and has more than double the three scored by Gonçalo Ramos, the club’s major summer signing.

Cisse was signed last winter and subsequently remained out on loan to Catanzaro. His season there ended in February due to an injury, yet Milan never left his side. If anything, credit goes to Amorim for placing his trust in him and integrating him from the very start, a gesture Cissé has repaid it.

He scored a goal on his debut against Torino, another against Juventus, and a brace against Bologna this past Wednesday. His three Europa League goals, meanwhile, all came on the same night in Salzburg.

Setting aside his international debut against Benfica – a match played by a makeshift side due to squad rotation – Alpha has not put a foot wrong in any game. Not even in the match against Lazio, a result that looks better in hindsight, given the Biancocelesti’s form.

Furthermore, it would be harsh to judge his performance as a centre-forward away at Bournemouth too negatively, as that display was clearly compromised by Maignan’s sending-off and the fact that the team fell behind by two goals, both from penalties.

Removing a player who is in a goal-scoring vein and fuelled by such enthusiasm could prove counter-productive, though the derby will bring more options, as both Rabiot and Moreira (who could slot into Cisse’s area of ​​the pitch) have been working toward their recovery since yesterday.

Two nights ago, Cisse operated as a number 10 – a link between the midfield and the penalty area – where he truly shone. While it’s true that Rabiot brings more experience to that central role, it’s equally possible that Adrien could drop back into the midfield alongside Modrić,.

Similarly, Cisse could start on the left, where he will face renewed competition from Moreira. Yet, Alpha possesses impressive stats, carried with the effortless grace of a young talent, one who now deserves the spotlight of the derby.

#2010. Savio scores on debut as Spurs cruise past Charlton in Carabao Cup

It looked like this was going to be a night for “one of their own”, but Tottenham Hotspur’s latest big-money arrival, Sávio, stole the headlines to crank up the excitement at his new club.

Mikey Moore had set Spurs on their way to what proved a comfortable Carabao Cup success over Championship club Charlton Athletic and heard his name sung by the home fans.

But Sávio stepped off the substitutes’ bench to take the limelight with a late goal just a few days after completing his expensive switch from Manchester City, and head coach Roberto De Zerbi is demanding many more to come.

“A perfect day for him,” said De Zerbi. “His biggest improvement is to increase the number of goals. He is one of the best wingers, but the best wingers score many goals and I spoke with him two days ago, and we put the goal at 10-12 goals.

“We need 10-12 goals from the wingers. Last season, we suffered too much because the number of goals were not enough.”

"What an introduction!"Sávio scores a brilliant goal on his Spurs debut! 👏 pic.twitter.com/WgmcfgeNpX

Having watched some of Tottenham’s signings fall to a 3-0 Premier League defeat by Brentford a few days earlier, Sávio’s late impact was the perfect lift for the Spurs supporters.

The club have committed to spending almost £400m this summer, leading to debate by outsiders over whether it will prove to be money well spent and huge waves of excitement within the fanbase.

A deal that could be worth as much as £85m, if add-ons are achieved, for Sávio certainly raised some eyebrows, but the Brazilian provided the perfect response by scoring just 11 minutes into his debut as a late substitute.

In the 82nd minute, Sávio cut in from the flank and scored with a shot past Charlton goalkeeper Tiernan Brooks. He and the Spurs crowd thought he had a second a few minutes later, but his shot hit Ben Davies on its way into the net and the defender was credited with the goal.

Having sung for Moore earlier in the game, the Spurs fans wasted no time in trying out their new song for Sávio, inspired by the Spandau Ballet hit Gold.

Moore has been expected to move to Cologne on loan, but provided a reminder of his talent by opening the scoring in the first half with only his second goal for the club.

What a hit from Mikey Moore! ⚪ pic.twitter.com/OgSM4qhiqs

“We have to understand the best solution,” De Zerbi said. “I would like to keep him. He’s young but a good player, but we can’t make the wrong decision. He needs to play, he needs to get games inside him.”

Cutting in from the right, where Sávio is primed to play, Moore surged past his marker and shot from just inside the box. Brooks should have stopped it, but the ball flew past him and into the net.

Three minutes after Moore’s opener, Dominic Solanke scored his first goal since March to offer a reminder of what he can still give De Zerbi, who is poised to welcome Omar Marmoush to Tottenham.

Buoyed by his first-half goal, Moore skipped his way around a couple of tackles at the start of the second period but his low cross was cut out. The Spurs fans responded by singing “he’s one of our own.”

Substitute Kevin Danso netted with his first touch from a header, before Sávio was introduced to steal the show, despite a late consolation goal from Charlton’s Lloyd Jones.

Kevin Danso scores with his first touch since coming on! ⚪ pic.twitter.com/oqUU7wjoJW

The victory set up a tough third-round trip to Anfield to face Liverpool for Tottenham, but De Zerbi said: “It’s a great game. If we want to win the competition we have to win the games.

“Sometimes in this competition, it can happen that you play against big teams. It’s a great challenge for the players, for me, for our clubs. We have to arrive ready to play in our style, with personality, ready to play a game following the work we are doing on the training ground.”

“He did great when he came on. He is going to be a joy for all of us to watch. I am sure he will be a fan favourite. He showed what a player he is tonight. To get one goal and an assist on his debut is great.”

Possession: Tottenham 73%-27% CharltonShots: 20-6Shots on target: 11-4Corners: 11-6Touches in opposition box: 45-8

It is all over in north London and Tottenham have booked their place in the third round of the League Cup with a comfortable 5-1 win over Charlton.

Newcastle have just about got past West Brom, winning 3-2 in the end, and they book their place in the third round.

At least the travelling Charlton fans have something to cheer about even if their side are being dumped out of the League Cup. A corner from the left comes to the back post, where Jones rises highest to head it between Kinsky’s legs and into the Tottenham net.

Savio thinks he has his second in quick succession but it will go down as Davies’ goal. Savio’s shot was on target but it deflects off Davies and goes in for Tottenham’s fifth on the night.

The Brazilian signed just yesterday but he now has a first Tottenham goal to his name. He cuts inside from the right and drives across the face of the penalty area before firing at the near post, beating Brooks. Tottenham are cruising into the third round and their newest signing scores on his debut.

"What an introduction!"Sávio scores a brilliant goal on his Spurs debut! 👏 pic.twitter.com/WgmcfgeNpX

Tottenham are cruising into the third round and so are Everton, who lead Preston by the same scoreline. Newcastle lead West Brom 3-2 whilst it is still 0-0 between Bradford and Burnley.

Change for Tottenham as Williams-Barnett replaces Tel.

Tel crosses from the left side of the box and picks out Savio, who attempts an audacious flick that does not come off.

West Brom were not back on level terms for long as Barnes has his second of the game and Newcastle lead 3-2 with under 10 minutes remaining.

Charlton have barely threatened the Tottenham goal tonight but that is a decent opportunity for Leaburn, who is played in down the right and forces Kinsky into a decent save.

Savio is straight into the action with good work down the right and squares it for Tel, whose shot is straight at Brooks.

Savio is on for his Tottenham debut and replaces Solanke. Savio only joined Tottenham yesterday but makes his first appearance for the club tonight.

Newcastle had fought from 1-0 down against West Brom to lead 2-1 but Hall has just given away a penalty for the second time in a matter of days having also conceded one in the dying moments of their 2-2 draw against Liverpool on Sunday. Price has stepped up to score his second of the game to bring West Brom level at 2-2 with just over 10 minutes to go.

The Austrian defender has just come on and, with his first touch, puts Tottenham 3-0 up. Fernandes’ free-kick from just outside the box on the right is met by Danso, who attacks it and his header finds the bottom corner. You have to say that goal was coming. Danso has hurt himself as there was a clash of heads as he met the delivery and receives treatment to his head.

Kevin Danso scores with his first touch since coming on! ⚪ pic.twitter.com/oqUU7wjoJW

Roberto De Zerbi is turning to his bench and making a triple change as Van de Ven, Danso and Porro come on.

Charlton are also making a triple change of their own.

Gray is found on the left side of the Charlton penalty area and he drives his shot towards goal, forcing Brooks into a decent save. Tottenham are pushing for that third goal.

A cross is sent in from the right and it comes to Tel, who volleys first time but it is a fairly routine save for Brooks in the Charlton goal.

Tottenham are starting to ramp up the pressure as they go in search of a third goal. As it stands, the only side that looks like scoring is Tottenham.

Plenty of cheers from the home fans as Savio is out to warm up. Will Roberto De Zerbi turn to the Brazilian and give him his debut tonight?

One of the new laws brought in this season is to speed up throw-ins and Gray falls foul of taking too long, with Charlton then being given the throw-in.

Tel decides to shoot from range after Charlton clear a corner but the Frenchman’s effort is straight at Brooks

Play has resumed in north London, with Tottenham 2-0 up over Charlton.

They are back under way at St James’ Park and there has been a goal within a few minutes of the second half starting. Newcastle were 1-0 down against West Brom but they now lead 2-1 thanks to Barnes’ goal.

Possession: Tottenham 76%-24% CharltonShots: 9-2Shots on target: 4-1Corners: 7-2Touches in opposition box: 25-2

The first half in north London is brought to an end and Tottenham take a 2-0 lead into the break thanks to goals from Moore and Solanke. Tottenham looked rather lethargic for a lot of that first half but two goals in quick succession has Roberto De Zerbi’s side in control. As the players head off, the DJ pays homage to the late Dolly Parton by blasting out Nine to Five.

Whilst they are still in added time in north London, it is half-time at St James’ Park and Newcastle are level 1-1 with West Brom.

Apter is booked for cynically tripping up Udogie.

Due to a few Charlton injuries, there will be six added minutes.

Like London buses, two goals come in quick succession and Tottenham have their second just before the break. Charlton fail to clear their lines inside their own box before Solanke volleys in on the swivel from the penalty spot. Charlton will feel that was definitely an avoidable goal.

Tottenham had looked rather lethargic but they take the lead in emphatic style. The 19-year-old cuts inside from the right and comes across the face of the Charlton penalty area. Moore then strikes it powerfully with his left foot and the ball flies into the roof of the net. Could Brooks have done better in the Charlton goal? Moore will not care.

What a hit from Mikey Moore! ⚪ pic.twitter.com/OgSM4qhiqs

Tottenham are currently too slow in possession and are not moving the ball quickly enough, meaning it is easier for Charlton to defend.

West Brom had taken the lead at St James’ Park but Newcastle are back on level terms through summer signing Toure.

A corner from the right ends up coming out to the edge of the box, where Tel takes it first time but his volley goes a long way wide. That moment sums up Tottenham’s evening thus far.

Solanke has a shot from the edge of the box blocked before Gray’s effort with the outside of his right foot is saved well by Brooks down to his left. That looked like it was creeping in so Brooks had to get a hand to that.

Charlton play the corner short and eventually the ball comes in. Asiimwe meets it and has a good chance from eight yards out but his header goes just wide. That was a decent chance for Charlton.

The first booking of the night goes the way of the hosts as Bergvall cynically takes down Apter as the Charlton man drove towards the Tottenham penalty area. You feel like Charlton need to take advantage of opportunities like this if they want to win this tie. The ball is clipped in and it comes off Van Hecke’s head for a corner. Tottenham clear their lines initially but Charlton keep it alive. Docherty strikes it first time from the edge of the Tottenham box and forces Kinsky into a good save diving to his left.

That probably sums up Tottenham’s night thus far. Davies pings a lovely diagonal ball out to Moore in space down Tottenham’s right. Moore waits for the overlapping run of Gray before playing the pass but Gray’s attempted cross from the right side of the box is terrible and goes behind for a goal kick. Roberto De Zerbi is quickly out of his seat!

Roberto De Zerbi was keen to see his side show a reaction to their defeat at Brentford on Saturday. Unsurprisingly, they are dominating possession but have not posed much of a threat going forward.

There has been a goal at St James’ Park and it is the visitors West Brom who have taken the lead over Newcastle. Price has scored directly from a free-kick and the Championship side lead.

A sensational free-kick from Isaac Price to give West Brom the lead at St. James' Park! 🤯Watch the Carabao Cup here! - https://t.co/4BMyhp9stB pic.twitter.com/Pnt78LWFN6

Things have just gone from bad to worse for Charlton. Whilst one of their centre-backs is being stretchered off in Sichenje, their other centre-half Koumetio, who used to be on the books at Liverpool, is also down. Koumetio, like Sichenje, is going to come off. McNamara and Jones, who like Koumetio used to be at Liverpool, are coming on. Charlton have had to change both centre-backs inside the opening quarter of an hour.

Sichenje did try to continue but he has gone back down again and his night appears to be over. The question will be has he done more damage to his knee trying to play on? The stretcher is being brought on and it will be a sorry end to his night.

Moore wins Tottenham a corner out on the right, which summer signing Fernandes will take. His delivery is headed away and the danger is gone.

Sichenje has now got back to his feet so he may have avoided a serious injury but we will see if he can continue. It looks like he will try to continue at least.

Play is halted as Charlton defender Sichenje looks to be in a lot of pain as he bangs the ground in frustration. It appears to be his left knee and the visitors may be forced into an early change.

Inside the opening minute, Solanke thinks he will have a chance on goal as the ball is played in behind but there is too much on it and the ball goes through to Brooks in the Charlton goal.

Both sides emerge from the tunnel at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium and we are just moments away from kick-off north London. Here is a reminder of how the two sides line up this evening:

Tottenham: Kinsky; Gray, Van Hecke, Davies, Udogie; Fernandes, Bentancur, Bergvall; Moore, Solanke, Tel. Substitutes: Dubravka, Robertson, Danso, Gallagher, Richarlison, Savio, Porro, Van de Ven, Williams-Barnett.

“Tottenham are a top club. Top manager and players so it is a wonderful opportunity to test ourselves. We need to be organised and in the moments we have we want to use our structure to carry a threat. We want to see our structure coming through because we want to evolve. We are a way off these yet, but that is eventually the goal.”

After nine years at Anfield, Andy Robertson has swapped Liverpool for Tottenham this summer. He started for Tottenham against Brentford and is on the bench tonight ahead of what could be his first home game for the club.

Omar Marmoush will undergo a medical at Tottenham Hotspur on Wednesday on loan with an obligation to pay Manchester City £60m for the Egypt forward next summer.

Marmoush will become the second signing from City this week after Savinho – who has asked to be referred to as Sávio – completed his move.

City signed Marmoush two seasons ago from Eintracht Frankfurt for £59m and the German club do not have a sell-on clause, meaning they will not receive a fee from the deal.

Our Spurs side to face Charlton! 📋🔢 @krakenfx pic.twitter.com/yQuEVgkHbm

A place in the League Cup third round is at stake as Tottenham host Charlton in a London derby at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium. The last competitive meeting between these sides came in the FA Cup back in January 2011, with Tottenham winning that game 3-0 at White Hart Lane. A then 19-year-old Andros Townsend made his debut that day and scored, with Jermain Defoe scoring a brace.

Tottenham’s Premier League campaign got off to the worst possible start as they lost 3-0 at Brentford last weekend. Tottenham have been very busy during this summer transfer window and that has continued this week. Savio (formerly Savinho) has arrived from Manchester City in a deal that could be worth £85m and the Brazilian could make his Tottenham debut tonight, having been registered in time.

“I think in attacking positions we need players capable one-on one, to create something, to create a chance to score,” Roberto De Zerbi said. “In terms of one-on-one, he [Savio] is one of the best players, especially since 2024. He can play on the right side, on the left side. I have known him from a long time, I spoke with him when he went to Manchester City. He is a big player for us.

“I do not know if I am the right man [to get the most out of Savio], but for sure he has to achieve. I think a player who is so good in one-on-one, so good at creating chances to score, to be complete, he has to score. If you analyse the other best wingers in the world, many of them, they score 10 to 15 goals per season. He has the qualities. Maybe his habits, he has to change habits, because he has to be focused on the assists, the one-on-one dribbling and also to score.”

Omar Marmoush is closing in on an initial loan deal from Manchester City but that move is not complete and thus he is not available for Tottenham tonight. Micky van der Ven and Pedro Porro are both available having missed Tottenham’s loss at Brentford but the hosts are still without Xavi Simons, Pape Sarr, Dejan Kulusevski and Wilson Odobert.

Charlton have made the perfect start to their Championship campaign; a 2-1 home win over Derby was followed up by a 2-1 victory at recently-relegated West Ham. Nathan Jones’ side earned their place in the League Cup second round with a 3-1 win at Cheltenham in the first round.

“We have to be very organised and very professional, they [Tottenham] are a top team,” Jones said. “They have a great manager and a brilliant group of players. They already had a Premier League squad and they have spent, what is reaching about, I do not know, £300 million or something like that. It is a wonderful test, we have to be right near our best and do both sides of the game very well. Of course, you want to test yourself against the best managers and you want to test yourself against the best teams. For us, this is not our priority, the Championship is our priority, but this is the next game and therefore it is the most important.”

#2007. Unseen moment Rangers star warned 'job's not done' by team-mate after semi-final win

Ivor Pandur delivered a stern warning to one of his Rangers team-mates after advancing to the final of the Premier Sports Cup.

The goalkeeper was caught telling Findlay Curtis to cool his celebrations at Hampden as he insisted the 'job is not done'.

Rangers posted a clip on social media of the players leaving the park in Glasgow after Ryan Naderi's late goal sent them through to the final. Rangers will face Hibernian next month.

🤩 Full-Time Scenes at Hampden! 💙 We're heading to the Final!! https://t.co/zOlCkZ6aKW

— Rangers Football Club (@RangersFC) October 31, 2026

And while the players were understandably jubilant as they were greeted by coaching staff and club staff as they left the park, Pandur wasn't allowing anyone to get carried away.

Curtis was passing the camera when he let out a loud celebratory cheer. Pandur then stepped in to motion to the young Scotland winger to calm down.

Pandur could then be seen and heard saying: "Easy bro, job is not done, bro."

After leading Rangers into the final, Derek McInnes commented: "I'd like to have enjoyed it a wee bit more. Enjoyment comes now, to be honest, a wee bit of satisfaction when I see the lads in the dressing room celebrating together.

"But the job now is to go and win the thing, and we'll get six weeks now between now and then where we need to get better at things I just spoke about.

"The players who are in the team at the minute need to play well to stay in the team if they want to be in the cup final, and the players who are not in the team need to keep performing and doing all they can to get in the team.

"We need to drive each other on because we want to get into the cup final on the back of some really strong league form.

"We're on a really strong run just now in terms of wins and being unbeaten over a period of time now. But we know we're not perfect.

"It's important that we keep searching for those improvements. But if we can keep winning, keep putting ourselves in cup finals and keep ourselves satisfied with results, we can keep working on performances."

#2006. Pedro Caixinha back in Europe after joining 13th club of managerial career

Former Rangers manager Pedro Caixinha has been appointed head coach of Cercle Brugge.

The Portuguese has signed a contract until June 2027, with the option of a further season, after the Belgian club parted company with Lars Friis.

Cercle Brugge beëindigt de samenwerking met Lars Friis. De Portugees Pedro Caixinha (55) volgt hem op als hoofdcoach van Groen-Zwart. De Vereniging bedankt Lars voor zijn inzet de voorbije maanden en wenst hem het allerbeste voor de toekomst. Met Pedro Caixinha haalt Cercle een coach met ruime internationale ervaring in huis. Hij tekent een contract tot juni 2027, met de optie op een bijkomend seizoen. 🔗 Lees meer via https://t.co/jsgsDLclPU

— Cercle Brugge (@cercleofficial) November 2, 2026

Cercle made the change after collecting six points from their opening 10 league matches, leaving them 17th in the table.

Caixinha, 55, spent seven months in charge of Rangers in 2017 during a managerial career that has taken him across Europe, South America, Mexico and the Middle East.

His most recent position was with Mexican club FC Juarez, while he has also managed Santos Laguna, Cruz Azul, Talleres, Red Bull Bragantino and Santos.

Caixinha won the league title, domestic cup and Supercopa MX with Santos Laguna and later lifted the Copa MX and Supercopa MX with Cruz Azul.

Ex-Rangers star calls time on playing career after 17 years

Rangers star called up by under-21 national team after being dropped from full squad

Cercle technical director Luciano Murchio said: “In Pedro, we welcome an experienced head coach who has demonstrated his qualities and achieved success at the highest level across different leagues and circumstances.

“We are convinced that he can help us achieve our objectives while respecting our playing principles and identity.

“We expect Pedro to have a positive impact on the team in the short term and help us turn around the current sporting situation.”

Caixinha will be assisted by Pedro Malta and Guilherme Gomes and will take charge of his first training session on Tuesday.

#2005. Ivan Toney's trial over assault at exclusive London nightclub will start in 20 MONTHS - putting England star's Euro 2028 prospects at risk

Published: 06:44 EDT, 29 October 2026 | Updated: 07:06 EDT, 29 October 2026

The assault trial of England international Ivan Toney will not be heard for another 20 months – potentially ruling him out of Euro 2028.

The trial will begin on June 12, 2028 - three days into the European Championships, which will take placed in the UK and Ireland - and is expected to last three to four days.

Toney, who was in this summer's World Cup squad, appeared at Southwark Crown Court for a pre-trial hearing on Thursday morning and pleaded not guilty to assault occasioning actual bodily harm.

The 30-year-old is accused of headbutting and punching Saber Da Silva at the 100 Wardour Street nightclub in Soho on December 6 2025.

Toney’s defence do not dispute that he caused the injury but claim he acted in self-defence.

Judge Christopher Hehir labelled the case ‘straightforward’ and apologised for the long wait until the trial. He cited the significant backlog in the judicial system, before warning Toney that it is a criminal offence not to turn up for the case.

Toney arrived at court at 9.10am on Thursday, flanked by a six-man entourage, wearing a black button-up cardigan with a white shirt, black tie and grey trousers. He will remain on bail until his trial.

Ivan Toney arrives at Southwark Crown Court for his hearing on Thursday morning

Toney was charged on July 31 after a Metropolitan Police investigation. When the charge was announced, a spokesperson for Toney said: ‘Ivan acknowledges the charge and although he is naturally shocked, he looks forward to being given the opportunity to clear his name in court.’

The England striker initially appeared at Westminster Magistrates' Court last month, where he opted to have his case heard by a jury at the Crown Court.

In October, the court heard that Toney and Da Silva ‘squared up’ before the striker ‘lunged forward and head-butted the complainant, followed by a few punches’.

The 30-year-old is currently plying his trade in Saudi Arabia for Al-Ahli and has scored 13 goals in 14 appearances this season. He left England for £40million in 2024, having scored 36 Premier League goals in 83 appearances for Brentford.

Toney started for England in their 6-4 World Cup bronze medal match against France but was left out of the most recent Three Lions squad.

#2004. Moreira lifts lid on Kaka-inspired number choice, first derby and friendship with Rabiot

Diego Moreira is gearing up for his first derby as an AC Milan player, and he is very much relishing the occasion.

Moreira was the second big splash in the summer window for Milan, after the club-record signing of Goncalo Ramos from Paris Saint-Germain. The Belgian has already impressed with three goals to his name, including a brace that rescued a draw against Lazio in the capital.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Having sat out of the last two games against Udinese and Bologna, the good news is that Moreira has recovered from his muscle issue and will therefore be available to the head coach Ruben Amorim for tomorrow night’s derby.

He spoke to DAZN in the ‘Remember The Name’ programme in an interview that was broadcast on the eve of the game, with his words relayed by MilanVibes.

“My name is Diego because it was my mother’s favourite name. She adored Diego Maradona and really liked it. When people analyse it, they say that with this name I seem to be made to play football, so I really like it.

“My Instagram name? My godfather’s name is Armizy on social media, and I copied it. I spend a lot of time with him. When I was little, I used to play football everywhere and break everything.

“My dream was to become a professional footballer, and we’re almost there, come on (laughs). I left home at 15, a very difficult time for my mother, but now we’re happy because I’ve achieved my dream of becoming a footballer, and the sacrifices we made have led to this.

“My mom is very important to me, she’s unique, and everything we’ve been through now makes us happy. I talk to dad often, and when I finish games and they don’t go well, I only talk to him because I know we’ll talk about football and nothing else.

“He was the one who called me and told me about AC Milan’s interest, he was just waiting for me to say yes or no. When AC Milan calls you, you can’t say no. My tattoos speak of my family, even my grandparents.”

You have spoken before about Hazard, Kaka and Cristiano Ronaldo…

“Eden is a gem. A champion, an inspiration: when you grow up watching him, you try his moves and hope to be able to do them on the pitch one day. Cristiano is my idol, a champion, the greatest.

“As a kid, I wanted to be him, to have my hair cut like him, but I had too much. He made me believe in myself and pushed me to play football. I’m happy to have enjoyed his prime.

“Kaka? I wanted number 7. When they told me it was available, I was tempted to take it, but I like number 22. I hope to honour it and do well enough to deserve this number.”

“Milan-Inter is one of the biggest derbies in Europe. We’re fired up, I’d die for my team and to play these games, we’re fired up.”

You have struck up a friendship with Rabiot…

“From the first few days, Adrien has been one of the ones who welcomed me best, especially because he speaks French.

“We talk a lot, especially because we’re always the last ones in the dressing room, so we often eat together and talk about life, football, everything. I also really enjoy being on the pitch, so that helps us get along.”

“The fact that I have a strong personality has helped me settle in. I feel great in this group and they understand me. We have to win games to bring Milan back to where it deserves to be: we have quality, spirit, a great group and we have to do it.”

#2003. Lamine Yamal's dad' 'almost smashes Russian blogger's phone' in bizarre row on streets of London after his Spain star son, 19, lost Ballon d'Or vote to Harry Kane - before Andriy Arshavin steps in!

Published: 07:54 EDT, 29 October 2026 | Updated: 07:57 EDT, 29 October 2026

Lamine Yamal's dad was embroiled in a bizarre spat with a Russian football blogger who attempted to speak to him outside of the Ballon d'Or awards on Monday.

Footage from content creator Seva Kryseva appeared to show him approaching Mounir Nasraoui, father of Barcelona sensation Yamal, while he was having a cigarette following the award ceremony in London.

Seemingly angry with the unsolicited approach, Nasraoui appeared to swipe at Kryseva's phone, causing him to back away.

The blogger then received a talking to from former Arsenal star Andrey Arshavin, who defended Nasraoui's actions.

Kryseva pleaded his innocence, insisting that Yamal's father was out of line, saying: 'Yamal's dad almost smashed my iPhone!' to which Arshavin quickly responded: 'He should've smashed your face in instead, Seva.'

Arshavin went on to say: 'Why are you bothering people? They lost—well, actually won the Little Ballon d'Or.' Before explaining that he himself had congratulated Nasraoui on his son's achievement earlier.

Kryseva tried to explain to Arshavin that he was only trying to do the same but said that: 'He was in a different mood. He was drunk, what do you expect?' The former Arsenal winger was not impressed by this excuse saying, 'you were bothering him with your phone.'

Yamal and his father might've been expecting to take the Ballon d'Or back to Spain but had to settle for a third Kopa Trophy in as many years

Yamal's father appeared to snatch the smack the blogger's phone out of his hand while being recorded

This all occurred after Yamal was awarded the Kopa Trophy, or as Arshavin calls it, the little Ballon d'Or, for best under-21 player in the world for the third year running.

But Yamal and his father might have been expecting the ultimate personal accolade to fall into the 19-year-old's hands after a stellar season that saw Yamal win a World Cup and LaLiga.

To exacerbate matters, at last year's awards in Paris, Yamal's father had already expressed his disappointment in his son not being awarded the Ballon d'or, claiming that he was the 'best player in the world by far.'

After the 2025 awards Nasraoui went on to say: 'I wouldn't say it was theft,' he said, 'but rather moral harm to a human being.'

Yamal's uncle Abdul fiercely defended his nephew on Cadena SER after he missed out on the Ballon d'Or

'Because I believe Lamine Yamal is the best player in the world. By far, by far. Not because he's my son, but because he's the best player in the world. He has no rival. He's Lamine Yamal.

'Something very strange happened here. Next year, he'll be the Spanish Ballon d'Or winner.'

And this year it was Yamal's uncle, Abdul, who suggested the award should have gone to the Barcelona winger in an interview with Cadena SER, in which he said: 'My nephew was fantastic, he was the best player in the world. Everyone knows it. If you love football, you go to see Lamine, not Harry Kane.

'Lamine has won a World Cup, La Liga,and the Super Cup. He plays very well. He's had an incredible season. He scores goals that no one else scores. Passes, assists, he has it all. He'll win five Ballon d'Or awards.'

#2002. Musah talks second chance at Milan, upcoming derby, Modric and other team-mates

The media coverage has ramped up into overdrive on the eve of the derby, with Yunus Musah the latest to speak ahead of the game.

Musah spent last season out on loan at Atalanta with Massimiliano Allegri not deeming him to be a part of his plans, but he returned in the summer as the Bergamo club did not use the option to buy. Many thought he would be packing his suitcases again, but that wasn’t the case.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Instead, the new head coach Ruben Amorim has placed a great deal of faith in the American, using him in a deeper midfield role which seems to be bringing out the best from him. He has previously spoken about feeling ‘grateful’ to have been given a fresh chance by Amorim.

Musah spoke in an interview with CBS Sports to preview Saturday night’s big game, one in which Milan really need three points in order to reduce the gap to the top of the standings. His words are via MilanNews.

“There’s still a long way to go, but after losing a season, I’ve learned that even in crucial moments, you have to keep going. Now I’m really keen to stay. I want to stay at this club and do really well here. The coach is helping me a lot, giving me opportunities that I need to seize.”

Considering what you went through last year, you’ve become the most used central midfielder this season: what instructions did the coach give you? What was the first thing he said to you when you spoke?

“Nothing complicated. The coaching staff works as a team, so the entire team knows exactly what each member is doing. They give us all the necessary instructions: how to receive the ball, how to read the various moments of the game, and how to interpret the play according to their instructions.

“This allows me to step onto the pitch without any hesitation. It’s a huge help, because when you step onto the pitch, you know exactly what you have to do.”

Can you better understand where you might not be recognised?

“For example, sometimes at the supermarket, when there aren’t many people, someone still stares at me, everyone wants to say hello or ask me something because everyone knows and watches AC Milan.

“Then, at a club where winning every single match is crucial, other teams approach AC Milan differently: for them, it’s the most important match of the season. Every match is difficult, everything has changed. Sometimes, to escape this celebrity aura, I go shopping at the supermarket at night.”

Knowing that Luka Modrić has been my favourite player for about 10-15 years, and given that you have the opportunity to train with him every day, what’s it like being around him?

“Yes, I try to enjoy the moment and the time I can spend with him. It won’t be many years, so I really appreciate every moment we spend together in midfield. In the past, when he played for Real Madrid, I managed to get a shirt.

“The world of football is really small, but now we find ourselves playing together, side by side in midfield. It’s unreal. It’s fantastic to share the dressing room with him, to be on the pitch with him.

“I’m learning so many things on the pitch just by watching him. Sometimes we speak Spanish, he speaks both English and Spanish well.”

“It’s a different game than the others. When you train for the derby, it’s more special. You don’t have to tell any of your teammates how important the game is or that they need to focus on it.

“Everyone is focused, working hard because it’s incredibly important for our fans, for us. It’s the game where, when you win, it’s like you’ve won a trophy. I’m very focused on this match.”

How difficult is it to focus on the games before the derby knowing that the match is so close?

“I think before the match, we all know the derby is close, but we’re focusing on the games we have to play first, then when the match comes, we’ll think about it. Clearly, it’s very important to win and take home the three points.”

Who did you grow up with as an AC Milan or Italian football idol? Who did you watch as a child?

“I really liked Ronaldinho, but I didn’t watch much football back then. I watched him more later, even through highlights. When I was little, I played football a lot more than I watched it. I enjoyed playing. Every day I’d go out with my brother and my friends and we’d spend hours playing.

“I love those days, out in the street playing. Anyway, Ronaldinho was a great player, and that’s why I chose the number 80 when I arrived at Milan.”

Who is most likely to become a coach after a playing career?

“Matteo Gabbia is truly tactically savvy.”

Who is most likely to become a social media influencer?

“I would have said Rafa but now I say Diego Moreira.”

Who is most likely to lose one of the three essential items: phone, wallet, or keys?

“Mario Gila always loses a lot of things, like on airplanes. Yes, definitely him. He needs those Apple gadgets, what are they called? AirTags! Yes, we need to give him some AirTags for Christmas.”

And who could survive the longest on a desert island?

“I’d say, I like it! I’m very resourceful, you know?

What’s the secret to surviving on a desert island? You seem very confident…

“I wouldn’t let the pressure get me down. I’d work hard, I’d try to find everything I needed to survive, I’d go fishing.”

The team most likely to win the Milan derby is?

#2001. The £3m-rated Scottish winger with 16-goal contributions after SPFL exit for nothing

Dinamo Bucharest president Andrei Nicolescu has revealed they will allow Scottish winger Danny Armstrong to leave the club for £3 million....just over a year after he left Kilmarnock for free.

The 29-year-old has scored six goals and provided ten assists in just 14 league games this season and has helped Dinamo reach the top of the Romanian league

His club are trying to win the title for the first time in 20 years, but Nicolescu admitted if an offer came in for Armstrong in January that was too good to turn down, they would have to accept it.

"So yes, if a bid came in for £3 million for him, he is definitely leaving because there is no way we can say no to an offer like that.

"That would still apply even if we were still challenging for the title.

"Let's be realistic. £3 million for a transfer of a player in Romanian football is a very large sum."
